# MSIL backend: implementation plan for Phases 0-3

Status: plan v2, 2026-10-12 (v1 revised after an adversarial review; dispositions in Appendix A); Phase 2 plan, 2026-10-21 (milestones M12-M23 and contracts 5.6-5.12, from the Phase 2 recon and the user's decisions of 2026-10-21, section 10); Phase 3 plan, 2026-10-28 (milestones M24-M35 and contracts 5.13-5.17, from the Phase 3 recon and the user's decisions of 2026-10-28, section 10). Owner: lead planner (agent farm). Base: branch `msil-milestone1` at `2829ef573b08` (the design-doc commit, rewritten 2026-10-13 from `8da03434abcc`; upstream base `d1e15b695381`); Phase 2: branch `msil` at `1ea64fe9fc7c` (after M11, with upstream llvm-project `64f50ffd4f1c` merged); Phase 3: branch `msil` at `cc4c79787d6a` (after M23; an upstream llvm-project merge follows this plan's commit and comes before M24, R21).
Inputs: [Design.md](Design.md) (settled decisions) and the recon reports in [recon/](recon/) (`triple-objfmt`, `registry-tm`, `clang`, `wasm-inventory`, `isel`, `passes-frame`, `asmprinter`, `cil-runtime`, `tests-ci`, `build-env`), plus [recon/artifacts/](recon/artifacts/): the experiment sources and logs behind `cil-runtime` and `build-env`, the `tests-ci` prototype, and the review experiments (`review-cil/`). Phase 2 inputs: the recon in [recon/p2/](recon/p2/) (11 reports and three judge reports; [decision-brief.md](recon/p2/decision-brief.md) is the synthesis), [Status.md](Status.md) and [TestCorpus.md](TestCorpus.md). Phase 3 inputs: the recon in [recon/p3/](recon/p3/) (11 reports with their experiments, the R5 addendum [r5-shared-state.md](recon/p3/r5-shared-state.md) and [decision-brief.md](recon/p3/decision-brief.md), the synthesis) and Status.md as Phase 2 built it. Every API, path and line number the plan relies on was checked in this checkout or comes from a recon report that checked it; anything else is marked *unverified*.

## 0. Summary

Phase 0 + Phase 1 of the MSIL backend as 11 small milestones (M0-M10), followed by M11, which closes the follow-ups of the first upstream merge, each one workflow run (parallel WPs on disjoint files -> one serialized build -> tests -> 3-lens review -> verified fixes -> gate -> one [MSIL] commit). M0 lands the build, plan-check, test and CI infrastructure with no LLVM changes. M1 front-loads every widely-included header edit (Triple.h, MCContext.h, MCObjectFileInfo.h, clang diagnostics) plus the clang TargetInfo wrapper, so the only full rebuild is M1 (a TableGen-only pre-build lets implementers syntax-check first). M2 creates the experimental MSIL target with every Phase-1 source file, final query hooks and stubs only for lowering hooks, so CMakeLists.txt, MSIL.h and the pass pipeline never change again. M3-M9 add capabilities in dependency order (leaf functions and stackification; calls, integers and select; FP; control flow; memory, frames and fences; globals and P/Invoke; function pointers, prototypes and aggregates). Every milestone's tests are written by separate test agents from the spec and only use capabilities that already exist (plan 5.5), and verification is enforced in every gate. M10 is the Design.md section 12 conformance gate (25+ programs at -O0/-O2 vs a native oracle, .NET 8/10/Framework, optimizing-JIT legs and a WSL Linux leg). Phase 2 (planned 2026-10-21 from the recon in recon/p2/ and the user's decisions, section 10) is M12-M23, with the same protocol and the shared contracts of sections 5.6-5.12: M12 fixes the backend items every linker path hits and adds the Linux native oracle; M13 front-loads every Phase 2 upstream hook and shared header (as M1 did for Phase 1) and builds lld; M14 links bitcode with msil-ld and adds the clang MSIL toolchain; M15 resolves P/Invokes from native libraries; M16-M17 build the ECMA-335 library (llvm/lib/CLI); M18 makes every MCInst one CIL instruction with a binary encoder; M19 writes CIL objects (ECMA-335 netmodules with a link-info record, Q1 = B2); M20 links CIL objects and writes the PE without ilasm; M21 binds the BCL from reference assemblies; M22 adds libraries and assembly-to-assembly linking; M23 is the Phase 2 exit (exit corpus, link-semantics matrix, objects by default). Phase 3 (planned 2026-10-28 from the recon in recon/p3/ and the user's decisions, section 10) is M24-M35, ordered by the real program each milestone unblocks (R1), with the same protocol and the shared contracts of sections 5.13-5.17, and with no front-loaded header milestone (R21); an upstream llvm-project merge comes first. M24 turns Phase 2's silent misbehaviour into errors, adds the trailer definitions and the narrow Phase 3 gate (R20); M25 builds compiler-rt's builtins as per-triple CIL archives (`clang_rt.builtins`); M26 adds variadic functions and acyclic dynamic allocas (zlib, c-testsuite's printing tests); M27 setjmp/longjmp through IL exception clauses (Lua); M28 native-callable function pointers and host-libc threads (`lua.c`); M29 `atexit`, global destructors and Windows start-up on the host C library's exit table; M30 atomics, whose lock path is the platform's library, and the SQLite shell; M31 `thread_local` and thread-exit destructors; M32 the cyclic shadow stack and architecture fallbacks; M33 codegen switches, exact BCL substitutions and i128 helpers; M34 structs by value at P/Invoke boundaries; M35 is the Phase 3 exit (zlib, Lua and SQLite on every runtime, both c-testsuite lists, the complete matrix). Phases 4 and 5 are outlined in section 7. Plan v2 addresses the adversarial review (Appendix A).

## 1. How agents use this plan

Each milestone is executed by **one workflow run**, then a human checks the result before the next run starts.

0. **Pre-spawn checks** (orchestrator, M1 on): `python msil/utils/plan-check.py ownership` (owned files are disjoint
   inside every milestone) and `python msil/utils/plan-check.py reads M<n>` (every input a WP is told to read exists).
   M0's inputs were checked by the planning run that wrote `recon/cil-runtime.md`, `recon/build-env.md` and
   `recon/artifacts/`.
1. **Plan and spawn.** The orchestrator gives each work package (WP) of the milestone to its own agent, together with
   sections 1-6 of this plan and the WP's `reads` list. Implementation WPs and test WPs run **in parallel**. A WP whose
   id ends in `.0` (for example M1.0) is a build-agent step: it owns no files and only writes the build tree.
2. **Ownership.** All agents share one working tree (`D:\llvm-msil`) and one build directory (`D:\llvm-msil\build`);
   there are no per-agent worktrees (disk and build time rule them out). A WP may create or edit **only** the files in
   its `owned_files` list (a path ending in `/` means every file under that directory). Ownership is per milestone: a
   later milestone may give the same file to a different WP. If a WP needs a change in a file it does not own, it stops
   and reports the exact change to the orchestrator; it never edits the file. The orchestrator itself may edit only this
   plan (amendments, section 12) and files under `llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/` (reviewer reports).
   - **2a. Dependencies.** `Depends on: X` (X in the same milestone) means: the WP is spawned with the others and
     writes its code against the section 5 contracts at once, but it may syntax-check or TableGen anything that
     includes X's files only after X has handed over, and it hands over only after those checks pass. Dependencies are
     acyclic. A WP that owns a header other WPs include writes the contract declarations first and keeps the header
     compilable after every edit, so a dependent's syntax check never fails on a half-written header.
   - **2b. Generator refresh.** When a hand-over changes TableGen input that a dependent compiles against, the
     generated files are refreshed before the dependent's checks: in M1 the build agent rebuilds the TableGen target
     (M1.0); from M2 on implementers run `msil-tblgen.ps1` into their own scratch directory.
3. **No builds by implementers.** Only the designated build agent runs `cmake` or `ninja`, through
   `msil-configure.ps1` / `msil-build.ps1` (exclusive lock). Implementers check their work with
   `msil-syntax.ps1` (compile one TU with `/Zs`, no outputs, no lock) and, from M2 on, `msil-tblgen.ps1`
   (TableGen into a scratch directory). Scratch files go under
   `<scratch>\milestones\<M>\<WP>\`, where `<scratch>` is the scratch directory the orchestrator
   passes to the milestone workflow (`C:\llvm-msil-scratch` since M11).
4. **Independent tests.** Test WPs are written by different agents than the implementation WPs they test, from the
   specification (Design.md, the recon reports, the contracts in section 5 of this plan), **without reading the
   implementation files of the same milestone**. Section 5.4 pins every structural record's operand list so MIR tests
   can be written from the spec. Tests use only capabilities that exist by their milestone (section 5.5).
   Exec-test `.expected` files are generated from a native build with `msil/utils/update-expected.py`, never
   hand-edited (per-OS overrides excepted, each with a comment).
5. **Serialized build, then tests.** When every WP has handed over, the build agent configures (if the milestone says
   so) and builds the milestone's target set; compile errors go back to the owning WP. Then the gate commands run.
6. **Adversarial review panel** with three distinct lenses, each reading the whole diff plus this plan:
   *CIL/semantic correctness* (does the emitted IL do what C and LLVM IR mean, on every runtime?), *LLVM conventions
   and maintainability* (coding standards, upstream idioms, minimal and mechanical diffs against WebAssembly, no stray
   upstream edits), and *test adequacy vs Design.md* (do the tests prove the milestone's goal, including negative
   cases?). Each milestone lists extra review focus points.
7. **Verified fixes.** A finding is fixed only after it is reproduced (a failing test or a concrete IL counterexample).
   The fix is made by an agent working within the same ownership rules; a test/implementation disagreement is settled
   against the specification, not by weakening the test.
   - **7a. Fix-loop ownership.** A verified fix may need a file that no WP of this milestone owns (for example
     `MSILTargetTransformInfo.cpp`, owned only in M2). The orchestrator may then assign that file to exactly one fix
     agent, after first adding a row to the section 12 amendment log whose Milestone column is `M<n>` and whose Change
     column reads ``fix-loop ownership: `<path>` -> <agent>`` (format in section 12). The scope check accepts such files
     for that milestone only.
8. **Gate and commit.** All gate commands pass (including the format and scope checks), then the orchestrator makes
   **one commit** on `msil-milestone1`: `[MSIL] M<n>: <milestone title>`, a body listing the WPs, the gate results and
   any amendments, and no Claude/AI attribution trailers (user instruction, 2026-10-13). The scope check (`plan-check.py scope
   M<n>`, last gate step) stages everything and accepts exactly: files owned by a WP of the milestone, files in that
   milestone's fix-loop amendment rows, and the allow-list `llvm/docs/MSIL/ImplementationPlan.md` and
   `llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/**`.
9. **Interface changes.** The names in section 5 are contracts. If one must change, the orchestrator records it in the
   amendment log (section 12) before the milestone's commit, so later milestones see it.

## 2. Conventions

- **Code:** [LLVM Coding Standards](../CodingStandards.rst); LLVM file header and license banner on every new file;
  `namespace llvm` with target helpers in `llvm::MSIL`, ISD nodes in `llvm::MSILISD`, TSFlags masks in `llvm::MSILII`;
  classes `MSIL<Name>`; legacy passes `MSIL<Name>Legacy` with `createMSIL<Name>LegacyPass()` and
  `initializeMSIL<Name>LegacyPass(PassRegistry &)`; `DEBUG_TYPE` and `cl::opt` names `msil-<kebab-name>`;
  `LLVM_ABI` on new public API in `llvm/include`. User-facing problems are diagnostics
  (`DiagnosticInfoUnsupported`, `LLVMContext::emitError`, clang `Diag`); `report_fatal_error` /
  `reportFatalInternalError` only for internal invariants (MSILStackCheck) and for stubs that later milestones replace.
- **Stubs vs query hooks (D33).** Only lowering hooks may be stubs: LowerOperation cases, LowerFormalArguments /
  LowerCall / LowerReturn, custom inserters, eliminateFrameIndex and AsmPrinter emit hooks. TargetLowering and TTI
  query hooks (`is*`, `should*`, `allows*`, `get*Ty`, `convert*`, `CanLowerReturn`) get their final bodies in M2,
  because the IR optimizer calls them through TTI at -O1 and above long before the code they describe exists.
- **Diagnostics leave well-formed output.** llc and clang keep running after a `DS_Error` (llc checks `HasErrors` only
  after `PM.run`, `llvm/tools/llc/lib/llcdriver.cpp:881-884`), so every path that diagnoses must hand later passes
  something valid that never reaches a stub: MSILPrepareIR deletes the body of a diagnosed definition and removes or
  neutralizes diagnosed globals; LowerCall for a diagnosed callee builds no call (it returns the chain and UNDEF
  results); other lowering hooks return a well-formed dummy value after the diagnostic. The visible result is the
  diagnostic and exit code 1, never `LLVM ERROR` or a stack dump.
- **Copied WebAssembly files** keep the upstream structure; the first comment after the banner is
  `// Derived from llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/<File> at d1e15b695381.` (the upstream base; files copied before 2026-10-13 say `8da03434abcc`, which has identical WebAssembly sources, and are corrected after M3); renames are mechanical
  (WebAssembly -> MSIL, wasm- -> msil-); wasm-only code is deleted, not commented out (decision D30).
- **Formatting:** clang-format (repo `.clang-format`, VS-bundled clang-format 22) on changed C++ lines; the gate runs
  `git-clang-format --extensions c,cpp,h,hpp,hxx,cxx,inc,cppm,cl --diff HEAD` over `llvm/lib llvm/include
  llvm/unittests clang/lib clang/include` (the extension list of `llvm/utils/git/code-format-helper.py`). `.td` files
  are never clang-formatted: git-clang-format would include them by default, and only `llvm/.clang-format` disables
  TableGen, not the root or `clang/.clang-format`. Tests are not clang-formatted.
- **Commits:** one per milestone on `msil-milestone1`, subject `[MSIL] M<n>: <title>`, body with WPs, gate results and
  any amendments. No Claude/AI attribution lines (no Co-Authored-By or 'Generated with' trailers; user instruction, 2026-10-13).
- **Tests:** lit tests use kebab-case names after the feature (`switch-i64.ll`, `frame-overalign.ll`); keep the
  WebAssembly name when porting (`reg-stackify.ll`, `function-bitcasts.ll`). llc tests always pass `-mtriple`, run
  both `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil` with a shared `CHECK` prefix (`LNX`/`WIN`
  where they differ), add `-verify-machineinstrs`, use `CHECK-LABEL: .method {{.*}}'<name>'(`, never contain a
  `target datalayout`, and end with `; RUN: %if ilasm %{ llc ... -o %t.il && %ilasm-verify -output=%t.dll %t.il %}`
  when they produce a full module. MIR tests are named after the behaviour they check (`stack-check-errors.mir`,
  `localloc-root.mir`) and use `-run-pass=msil-<pass>` with the operand lists of section 5.4. A test that expects a
  user diagnostic runs `not llc ... 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --implicit-check-not="LLVM ERROR"
  --implicit-check-not="PLEASE submit"`: on Windows `report_fatal_error` ends in `abort()` (exit code 3), which plain
  `not` accepts as a failure, so only the output shows a crash. Internal errors (MSILStackCheck) use `not --crash`.
  Gate commands that expect an error use `msil-expect-error.ps1` for the same reason. clang tests that run the backend
  have `// REQUIRES: msil-registered-target`; frontend-only tests have none. Unit tests live in
  `llvm/unittests/Target/MSIL/MSIL<Topic>Test.cpp` and every new gtest name contains `MSIL`; gates that must prove a
  gtest ran (not skipped) use `msil-gtest.ps1 -NoSkip -MinTests N`. Execution tests follow section 5.5.
- **Installs:** the user pre-approved installing build and test tooling (2026-10-12): NuGet packages, dotnet tools,
  pip packages, WSL apt packages. Prefer what is already installed (section 8); name every install (package and
  version) in the hand-over. Never add a download to a gate or build script without a WP owning that change.
- **Never:** read or copy
  `%APPDATA%\NuGet\NuGet.Config`; edit `llvm/docs/MSIL/Design.md`; run `ninja check-llvm`, `check-clang` or `check-all`;
  modify upstream GitHub workflows.

## 3. Settled decisions (lead planner)

Recon reports disagreed in a few places or left questions open. These are the binding answers for Phase 1. Items that genuinely need the user are in section 10; until the user answers, the default given here applies. Phase 2 amends some of these decisions through section 12 rows dated 2026-10-21 (D3, D5, D9, D10, D12, D14, D19, D21, D22, D26, D27, D28, D30, D31, D33, D36, D38); D12, D14 and D26 also carry a Phase 2 note in place (decision brief section 3 item 20). Phase 3 amends D2, D7, D13, D19 and D26 through section 12 rows dated 2026-10-28 or later, and D16, D21 and D36 carry a Phase 3 note in place (Phase 3 decision brief, sections 3.2 and 8, R10 and R11).

| # | Topic | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | TableGen form | **One record per instruction** (wasm-inventory 3.3), not the register/stack dual form of isel.md 10.1. Nothing in Phase 1 consumes stack forms; `_S` twins can be added mechanically if phase 2 wants an `.il` parser. WebAssembly record names are kept where semantics match, so copied passes compile unchanged. |
| D2 | 64-bit values | Register class `I64` (pointers and 64-bit integers) is CIL **`native int`** everywhere on 64-bit triples: locals, params, results, evaluation stack. `int64` is never emitted (PEVerify flags native int/int64 mixing). `CONST_I64` prints `ldc.i4 N; conv.i` or `ldc.i8 N; conv.i`. |
| D3 | Triple API | Add exactly `Triple::MSIL`, `isOSBinFormatMSIL()`, `getDefaultObjectFormat()` and `getNativeFormatTriple()`. `computeDataLayout` of an MSIL triple is the native triple's (byte-identical). `getDefaultExceptionHandling()` is None; `getDefaultLongDoubleFormat()` is IEEEdouble. `normalize()` is unchanged (`x86_64-pc-win32-msil` -> `x86_64-pc-windows-msil`). `supportsCOMDAT()` stays true; the backend ignores comdats (D26). |
| D4 | Target selection | Option A of registry-tm.md 1.2: only `TargetRegistry.cpp` changes; the target is named `msil`, never matches an arch, is chosen for every MSIL triple, and `-march=msil` switches the object format. |
| D5 | MC environment | `MCContext::IsMSIL` + header-only `MCSectionMSIL` + `MCContext::getMSILSection` + `MCObjectFileInfo::initMSILMCObjectFileInfo` (triple-objfmt.md 4). |
| D6 | Phase-1 triples | clang: x86_64 and aarch64 on Linux (gnu, musl) and Windows (msvc, gnu). `*-apple-darwin*-msil` and `i686-*-msil` are rejected as unknown triples until phases 4/5 (they need the UserLabelPrefix rework for `m:o`/`m:x`). Backend: x86_64 and aarch64 MSIL triples. Execution: `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil` on Windows, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil` under WSL (.NET 10). |
| D7 | Subtarget | One processor `generic`, no features; every native CPU/feature string from clang is accepted silently; native strings are kept on the subtarget for later SIMD mapping. |
| D8 | TTI / codegen options | MSILTTIImpl: 0 vector registers, no lookup tables (`shouldBuildLookupTables()` false: SimplifyCFG would otherwise turn switches of constants into `@switch.table` globals plus loads, `BasicTTIImpl.h:644-648`) and no relative lookup tables, no partial/runtime unroll. `Reloc::Static`, `CodeModel::Small`, `TrapUnreachable = true`, `NoTrapAfterNoreturn = false`, `EmitAddrsig = false`, `ExceptionModel` forced to None whatever the driver passes (clang's MinGW toolchain passes `-exception-model=seh` even for C), `usesPhysRegsForValues() == false`. TargetLowering and TTI query hooks are final in M2 (D33). |
| D9 | Build configuration | Keep the build-env configuration: targets `X86;WebAssembly` + experimental `MSIL`, projects `clang;lld` (lld unused in Phase 1), clang-cl/lld-link, Release + assertions, `LLVM_OPTIMIZED_TABLEGEN=OFF`. No AArch64 backend (MSIL is selected by object format; clang's AArch64 TargetInfo is always built). |
| D10 | Assembly references | Phase 1 emits only `.assembly extern mscorlib { .publickeytoken = (B7 7A 5C 56 19 34 E0 89 ) .ver 4:0:0:0 }` and uses only mscorlib members (`Marshal::AllocHGlobal`, `Marshal::StringToHGlobalAnsi`, `Environment::GetCommandLineArgs`, `Buffer::MemoryCopy`, `Interlocked::MemoryBarrier`). Verified to run unchanged on .NET 8/9/10 and .NET Framework 4.8 (cil-runtime e01/e01c; isel fence experiment). No `DisableRuntimeMarshalling` (blittable `preservesig` signatures do not need it). There is no core-library switch and no target-framework option: from P2-B on, msil-ld is given reference assemblies and binds every BCL type and member the generated code needs by searching them, so .NET 8 reference assemblies give references such as System.Runtime, System.Runtime.InteropServices and System.Threading, and .NET Framework's give mscorlib (section 12, 2026-10-14). |
| D11 | Identifiers and labels | Every symbol-derived identifier is single-quoted through `MSIL::printQuotedName` (escapes: `\'`, backslash as `\134`, control bytes as octal, UTF-8 raw plus a BOM when any global name is non-ASCII). Compiler-generated names use the `<msil>` prefix (no dots in type names). Block labels are `@BB<f>_<b>` (`InternalSymbolPrefix = "@"`). Names come from IR names, never from the Mangler. |
| D12 | Globals | One unmanaged data segment per module, allocated and filled by `<Module>::.cctor` from an RVA blob, with straight-line relocations and ctors; one `initonly native int` address field per global; code uses `ldsfld native int 'g'` (+ `ldc.i4 off; add`). Initializer bytes are captured from `AsmPrinter::emitGlobalConstant` through a collector streamer (NVPTX-style walker as fallback). RVA memory is never written and `&(label)` data is never emitted. **Phase 2 (decision brief item 20; section 12, 2026-10-21):** one data segment per module holds only for `-S` and llc text; CIL objects carry one record segment per defined global (5.8.8), and msil-ld outputs get one segment per assembly, laid out by `cli::layoutImage` from the objects' segments (5.9.9, M20). |
| D13 | Frames | Design.md 4.2: one `localloc` at entry sized for the static frame, FP as a fake physreg turned into a vreg, `.locals` never `init`. The assumed localloc alignment is **8 bytes** (`MSILFrameLowering::getLocallocAlign()`): constant-size localloc of 32 bytes or less is only 8-aligned on .NET Framework 4.8 and in .NET 8 tiered code (review experiment `recon/artifacts/review-cil/align16.il`; the recon had measured only variable sizes), so any frame with MaxAlign > 8 (`__int128`, `_Alignas(16)`, arrays clang aligns to 16) over-allocates MaxAlign - 8 bytes and aligns up. Dynamic alloca, stacksave/stackrestore and frameaddress are diagnosed in Phase 1 (shadow stack in phase 3). The frame model stays behind one helper (user decision on a value-type frame pending, section 10). |
| D14 | P/Invoke (Phase-1 import table) | An undefined function referenced from code or data becomes `pinvokeimpl("<lib>" cdecl) ... preservesig` only if it is a Phase-1 import: `puts` and `putchar` from the C library (linux-gnu/linux-musl `libc`, windows-msvc `ucrtbase`, windows-gnu `msvcrt`); the C math functions clang or the legalizer emit (sqrt, cbrt, floor, ceil, trunc, round, rint, nearbyint, fmod, remainder, fma, fmin, fmax, fdim, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, exp, exp2, expm1, log, log2, log10, log1p, pow, ldexp, frexp, modf, hypot, and their `f` variants) from the math library (linux-gnu `libm.so.6`, because glibc keeps libm separate and CoreCLR special-cases only `"libc"`; linux-musl `libc`; windows-msvc `ucrtbase`; windows-gnu `msvcrt`); or any function carrying the `msil-import-module` attribute (`msil-import-name` sets the entry point). Every other undefined function is an error: Phase 1 has no linker, and Design.md 5.2 step 4 makes an unresolved symbol a link error, not a runtime failure. Variadic callees are errors. Library calls whose name starts with `__` (compiler-rt and `__atomic_*` helpers) are errors until phase 3. **Phase 2 (decision brief item 20; section 12, 2026-10-21):** this table is the standalone import policy of `clang -S` and llc, frozen until the end of Phase 2 (no entry added or removed; 5.10.13). msil-ld's linked output resolves undefined functions from native libraries instead (M15, Q13), and object mode has no import policy: undefined functions become object symbols (M19). C spells the two attributes with WebAssembly's `import_module` and `import_name` (Q35, M13), and from M18 every P/Invoke prints `nomangle cdecl` (Q13, 5.10.11). |
| D15 | Memory intrinsics | Never libcalls. Constant-length memcpy <= 2^32-1: `cpblk`; memset: `initblk` (variable length truncated with `conv.i4`, documented 4 GiB limit); memmove and variable-length memcpy: `[mscorlib]System.Buffer::MemoryCopy(void*, void*, int64, int64)` (NativeMemory is net6+ only). |
| D16 | BCL intrinsics | None in Phase 1: ctlz/cttz/ctpop/bswap/rotates use LLVM's generic arithmetic expansions; fabs, copysign and FP<->integer bitcasts use the generic expansions through a stack slot and therefore work from M7 (their tests live in M7). isel.md decision 11 becomes phase-3 codegen switches that permit specific newer APIs, with defaults that run on .NET Framework 4.8 and modern .NET alike and, where that is possible, capability also taken from the reference assemblies (P2-B). A changed behaviour cannot be read from the references: `Math.Min`/`Max` order signed zeros only on modern .NET (isel.md 3.2), so the switch that maps fminimum/fmaximum to them alone decides, and by default they keep their M5 compare-and-select lowering. There is no net8.0 profile (section 12, 2026-10-14). **Phase 3 (R9 and R10, user decisions 2026-10-28; 5.16, M33):** the codegen switches are MSIL target features (`-mmsil-<name>`) plus msil-ld options, all off on every triple; `msil-minmax` is the switch that maps fminimum/fmaximum to `Math.Min`/`Max`. Exact BCL substitutions need no switch and become defaults once a 10^7-input property test passes bit for bit on every runtime (5.16.7): `Math.Sqrt`, `Floor`, `Truncate`, `Round` and `Abs` for `sqrt`, `floor`, `ceil` (as `-Math.Floor(-x)`), `trunc`, `rint`/`nearbyint`/`roundeven`, `round` and `fabs`, `BitConverter` for the f64 bit casts and trailer definitions for the f32 ones. A member that fails keeps its lowering, and libm's functions stay host P/Invokes. |
| D17 | uint64 -> FP | Custom for f32 and f64 results. `LowerUINT_TO_FP` emits `s = srl x, 63; y = or (srl x, trunc s), (and x, s); r = sint_to_fp y; result = fmul r, sint_to_fp(add s, 1)`: compiler-rt's halving with a sticky bit, with no SELECT and no memory. `conv.r4`/`conv.r8` of a non-negative int64 round once on every runtime (cil-runtime e05b) and the multiply by 1 or 2 is exact, so the result is correctly rounded. Never `conv.r.un` for 64-bit inputs (it double-rounds on .NET 8/9 and Framework, e05), and never the generic expansions (BITCAST through a stack slot for f64, SELECT for f32). |
| D18 | Calls | WebAssembly's `CALL_PARAMS`/`CALL_RESULTS` split and custom inserter; signatures from `computeSignatureVTs`; `calli` signatures from the MI; MSILFixFunctionBitcasts required but **without** WebAssembly's main renaming. |
| D19 | Varargs | Variadic definitions and calls are diagnosed in Phase 1 (phase 3 implements Design.md 4.7). |
| D20 | .maxstack | Computed and verified by MSILStackCheck (last machine pass, always on, fatal on violation) with the `StackPeakExtra` TSFlags field. |
| D21 | Verification policy | A test passes verification when MSILStackCheck, `jitall` (force-JIT every method under time and memory limits), ILVerify with a code allow-list (`Unverifiable`, `InitLocals`, `StackByRef`, `UnmanagedPointer`) and, on Windows, PEVerify with its allowed messages are all clean. PEVerify's `[found Native Int][expected unmanaged pointer] Unexpected type on the stack.` is allowed because `Buffer::MemoryCopy(void*, void*, int64, int64)` takes native int addresses (D15; review experiment `ilv2.il`); every other `Unexpected type on the stack` stays fatal. Enforced in every gate from M0 (`msil_require_verify=1`, D38). This replaces the literal 'ilverify reports no stack-shape errors' (ILVerify stops at the first error per method and cannot verify `calli`); user approval pending, section 10. **Phase 3 (5.17.16; R11, user decision 2026-10-28):** EH filter and fault clauses (M27, M32; no new message), delegate construction `ldnull; ldftn; newobj D::.ctor(object, native int)` (M28; pass 2 keeps that `ldftn`), and `Interlocked` members called on a native int address (M30; pinned by the listing, stubbed in pass 2). Each part enters msil-verify.py with the milestone that first emits its shape; any other verifier message is a defect or a new question for the user. |
| D22 | Runtimes in tests | .NET 8 by default; .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8 legs in the gates where runtime behaviour differs (FP, conversions, frames, globals) and in M10; WSL .NET 10 for the Linux triple; optimizing-JIT legs with `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0` (D38). |
| D23 | Pass manager | Legacy pipeline only in Phase 1. Copied passes drop their new-PM wrapper classes; `MSILPassRegistry.def` and `MSILCodeGenPassBuilder` are phase 4. |
| D24 | Memory flags | A post-ISel `MSILSetMemFlags` pass (modeled on WebAssemblySetP2AlignOperands) fills a memflags immediate (bits 0-2 unaligned N in {1,2,4}, bit 3 volatile), not a root-aware ComplexPattern. |
| D25 | Stack protector | MSILPrepareIR strips `ssp`/`sspstrong`/`sspreq`/`safestack` with a warning (the Linux and MSVC toolchains default to no protector anyway). |
| D26 | Linkage | linkonce/weak/comdat definitions are ordinary definitions in the single-module world (MSVC string literals `??_C@...` included). External global variables, `thread_local`, aliases, ifuncs, non-empty `llvm.global_dtors` and module asm are errors. **Phase 2 (decision brief item 20; section 12, 2026-10-21):** in whole-program mode (`-S`, llc text and msil-ld's `--lto-emit-asm` text) M12 lowers aliases of defined functions and variables, makes an unresolved `extern_weak` null plus a trap stub, turns a section on a global variable definition into an error (until M20, from which whole-program output lays out named sections as a one-object link does) and drops unreferenced discardable functions; in object mode (M19) aliases, `extern_weak` declarations and external globals become object symbols (5.8.10). Non-empty `llvm.global_dtors`, `thread_local`, ifuncs and module asm stay errors. |
| D27 | Entry point | `'<msil>Main'(string[])` with `.entrypoint`: calls `main()` directly, or builds a NULL-terminated argv from `Environment.GetCommandLineArgs()` (argv[0] = dll path) for `main(int32, native int)`; any other signature is an error. |
| D28 | Assembly name | `-msil-assembly-name`, default the stem of `source_filename`. The harness runs every DLL from a private directory, so same-named assemblies never collide. |
| D29 | Method text | One-line header `.method <public|assembly> static <ret> '<name>'(<params>) cil managed`, `{` on the next line, `.maxstack`, optional `.locals (...)`, body, and `} // end of method '<name>'` (the update_llc_test_checks regex depends on it). |
| D30 | Copied files | Copy only the curated COPY/ADAPT set (wasm-inventory 4.4), never wholesale; derivation line in every copied file; diffs kept mechanical for future merges. |
| D31 | ilasm | Default ilasm on Windows is .NET Framework ilasm 4.8 (`-nologo -quiet -dll -pe64 -x64`); modern ilasm 10.0.12 from the local NuGet cache is a second leg in M10; Linux CI uses the NuGet ilasm. |
| D32 | Early exec tests | Until frames exist (M7), every C execution test uses `%{msil_c_O2}` with the first-line comment '-O0 needs frames (M7)': clang -O0 always puts parameters and locals in allocas, and on windows-msvc even `int main(void){return 42;}` gets a return-value alloca and a store. `.ll` tests through llc carry the -O0 coverage before then. M7.d switches every earlier C test to `%{msil_c}`. |
| D33 | Stubs | M2 creates every Phase-1 `.cpp`/`.h`, so CMakeLists.txt, MSIL.h and the pipeline never change again in Phase 1. Only lowering hooks are stubs (they fail loudly naming the milestone that implements them); query hooks are final in M2 (section 2). |
| D34 | Select (M4) | ISD::SELECT is Legal from M4 through `SELECT_<RC>` pseudos expanded by the custom inserter `emitSelect` into a brtrue triangle with a PHI (isel.md 11.6). Generic legalization emits SELECT long before control flow exists (variable-amount i128 shifts via expandShiftParts, min/max expansions), so it cannot wait for M6. `convertSelectOfConstantsToMath` returns true (final in M2), so sext/zext of a compare stays arithmetic instead of becoming select(setcc, -1, 0) (`DAGCombiner.cpp` ~16088). |
| D35 | Switch index | `getJumpTableRegTy` returns i32 (NVPTX precedent), so every jump table indexes with int32 and only `BR_TABLE_I32` exists: CIL `switch` on a native int fails ILVerify with StackUnexpected (review experiment `sw.il`). SelectionDAGBuilder range-checks the full-width value before truncating, so 64-bit switch values stay correct (they print `conv.i4` before `switch`). LLVM's range check is never removed. |
| D36 | Fences | A singlethread fence (clang's translation of `asm volatile("" ::: "memory")`) selects the generic `MEMBARRIER` pseudo (AArch64 precedent; printed as the comment `// MEMBARRIER`; RegStackify does not move memory operations across it). Any other fence calls `[mscorlib]System.Threading.Interlocked::MemoryBarrier()`. Atomic loads, stores and RMW stay unsupported until phase 3. **Phase 3 (decision brief 3.2; 5.14.4, 5.15.6):** from M24 a singlethread fence, `atomic_signal_fence` and an empty `asm` with a memory clobber call the private trailer definition `__msil_compiler_barrier` (`noinlining`, body `ret`) instead of the `MEMBARRIER` comment, which the JIT does not see (spin loops hung on Framework, .NET 8 with TieredCompilation=0 and .NET 10); system fences keep `Interlocked::MemoryBarrier()`. From M30 atomics of 1-8 bytes are inline `volatile.` accesses and `Interlocked` calls, and 16-byte, generic-size and misaligned ones take the platform's process-wide lock path (`libatomic.so.1` on Linux triples, the MSVC STL's `msvcp140_atomic_wait.dll` on Windows triples; user decision R5, 2026-10-28). |
| D37 | Exit codes and checks | Test exit statuses are 0..255 on every OS: Linux truncates to 8 bits, so a larger Windows value would make the WSL leg pass by accident. Bitmask tests use at most 8 bits; programs mask their checksum (`& 0xff`). Before M6 (no branches) C tests accumulate results with the branch-free `MSIL_CHECK(acc, bit, cond)` and `return acc;`; `MSIL_EXPECT` is used from M6 on. `main` always returns explicitly (`-Werror=return-type`, because `-ffreestanding` disables main's implicit `return 0`). The harness and update-expected.py reject out-of-range statuses. |
| D38 | Enforced verification and optimizing-JIT legs | Every gate passes `msil_require_verify=1`, so a missing ILVerify, jitall or (Windows) PEVerify is a configuration error rather than UNSUPPORTED. Because short tests run almost entirely as Tier-0 code, the gates add `msil_dotnet_env=DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0` legs: 02-fp in M5, 04-frames and 05-memory in M7, and all of msil/test/M1 on Windows .NET 8 and WSL .NET 10 in M10. |

## 4. Build configuration and command reference

```text
Host: Windows 11, i7-7700K (4 cores / 8 threads), 64 GB RAM, VS 2026 Professional (clang-cl 22.1.3, lld-link, llvm-lib, CMake 4.3.1 inside the dev env), ninja 1.13.2, Python 3.14.7. Build dir D:/llvm-msil/build (gitignored, already configured by the build-env recon). Until M0 lands the helper scripts live in D:/llvm-msil/build/msil-scripts/ (same names, same arguments); M0 moves them to D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/ and everything below uses that path.

Configure (build agent only):
  M0, M1:   pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-configure.ps1
  M2 on:    pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-configure.ps1 -Experimental MSIL
  (M0 adds -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_PROJECTS=msil -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_MSIL_SOURCE_DIR=D:/llvm-msil/msil to the script's defaults.)
Equivalent raw command, inside the VS x64 dev environment:
  cmake -G Ninja -S D:/llvm-msil/llvm -B D:/llvm-msil/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON -DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS="clang;lld" -DLLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="X86;WebAssembly" -DLLVM_EXPERIMENTAL_TARGETS_TO_BUILD=MSIL -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_PROJECTS=msil -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_MSIL_SOURCE_DIR=D:/llvm-msil/msil -DLLVM_OPTIMIZED_TABLEGEN=OFF -DLLVM_PARALLEL_COMPILE_JOBS=8 -DLLVM_PARALLEL_LINK_JOBS=2 -DLLVM_ENABLE_PDB=OFF -DLLVM_INCLUDE_BENCHMARKS=OFF -DLLVM_INCLUDE_EXAMPLES=OFF -DLLVM_INCLUDE_TESTS=ON -DLLVM_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DLLVM_APPEND_VC_REV=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_ZLIB=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_ZSTD=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_LIBXML2=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_DIA_SDK=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=OFF -DCLANG_ENABLE_STATIC_ANALYZER=OFF -DCLANG_ENABLE_OBJC_REWRITER=OFF -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=<python.exe, forward slashes> -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Professional/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/clang-cl.exe" -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Professional/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/clang-cl.exe" -DCMAKE_LINKER="C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Professional/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/lld-link.exe" -DCMAKE_AR="C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Professional/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/llvm-lib.exe" -DLLVM_ENABLE_LLD=ON
  (Python3_EXECUTABLE must use forward slashes; MSIL goes only in LLVM_EXPERIMENTAL_TARGETS_TO_BUILD, never LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD.)

Build (build agent only; serialized by the orchestrator; long builds run with run_in_background and the agent waits; the script takes an exclusive file lock and throttles -j when RAM is low):
  pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-build.ps1 <targets>
  M1 target set:   llc opt clang FileCheck not count split-file llvm-config TargetParserTests MCTests
  M2+ target set:  llc opt clang FileCheck not count split-file llvm-config MCTests MSILTests
Lit (shared lock, source-tree paths):   pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-lit.ps1 [-LitArgs "-sv --param k=v"] <paths>
Run one built tool (shared lock):        pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-run.ps1 llc -mtriple=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil in.ll -o -
Syntax-check C++ without ninja (any agent, lock-free):  pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-syntax.ps1 [-FlagsFrom <tu>] [-ExtraInclude <dirs>] <files>
TableGen check without ninja (any agent, M2+):           pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-tblgen.ps1 -Out <scratch dir>
gtest with skip/count checks (gates):                     pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-gtest.ps1 -Exe <test.exe> -Filter <pattern> [-NoSkip] [-MinTests N]
Expect a clean diagnostic, not a crash (gates):            pwsh -NoProfile -File D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-expect-error.ps1 -Pattern <regex> -- <exe> <args>
Plan checks (orchestrator and gates):                      python D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/plan-check.py ownership | reads M<n> | scope M<n>
Milestone pre-spawn (orchestrator, M1 on):                 python D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/plan-check.py ownership && python D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/plan-check.py reads M<n>
Unit tests: D:/llvm-msil/build/unittests/Target/MSIL/MSILTests.exe; D:/llvm-msil/build/unittests/TargetParser/TargetParserTests.exe; D:/llvm-msil/build/unittests/MC/MCTests.exe
Format check: pwsh -NoProfile -Command "Set-Location D:/llvm-msil; git add -A; python 'C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Professional/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/git-clang-format' --binary 'C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Professional/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/clang-format.exe' --extensions c,cpp,h,hpp,hxx,cxx,inc,cppm,cl --diff HEAD -- llvm/lib llvm/include llvm/unittests clang/lib clang/include"  (must print no diff; same extension list as llvm/utils/git/code-format-helper.py, so .td files are never formatted)
Never: ninja check-llvm / check-clang / check-all (they build every tool); LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD=MSIL (fatal); LLVM_OPTIMIZED_TABLEGEN=ON with assertions (nested native build); a second build tree on D: (34 GB free).
```

Rebuild costs (step counts from `ninja -t commands` in the build-env recon; times are estimates on this shared 4C/8T host): M1 target set 3,462 steps (2,762 C++ TUs, 242 tablegen runs), 1-2.5 h; the whole tree 4,817 steps. After M1 only the MSIL target and relinks are rebuilt (5-30 min). The build script drops to `-j 4` below 16 GB free RAM and `-j 2` below 6 GB, because other agents' .NET experiments have been seen holding 40 GB.

## 5. Shared contracts

Sections 5.1-5.5 are the Phase 1 contracts. Sections 5.6-5.12 are the Phase 2 contracts (2026-10-21): 5.6 source layout and ownership, 5.7 the ECMA-335 library, 5.8 CIL objects and the link-info record, 5.9 msil-ld, 5.10 the driver and native imports, 5.11 BCL reference binding, 5.12 the Phase 2 test harness and gates. Where a Phase 2 milestone changes a contract (Phase 1's included), a section 12 row dated 2026-10-21 or later says so, and the row wins over the text it amends. Sections 5.13-5.17 are the Phase 3 contracts (2026-10-28): 5.13 source layout, ownership and the IR pass pipeline, 5.14 private helpers and the link-info record v1.x, 5.15 the runtime ABI, 5.16 codegen switches, 5.17 the Phase 3 test harness, gates, corpus and CI. Where they replace an earlier contract they say so (5.17.1 for 5.12); every other change of earlier text is a section 12 row dated 2026-10-28 or later.

### 5.1 ILAsm output contract (Phase 1)

Everything `llc`/`clang -S` prints for an MSIL triple has this shape. Tests are written against it, the `MSILTargetStreamer` and `MSILInstPrinter` produce it, and `update_llc_test_checks.py` parses it.

```text
// MSIL module generated by LLVM
// source_filename = "prog.c"
// target triple   = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil"
.assembly extern mscorlib { .publickeytoken = (B7 7A 5C 56 19 34 E0 89 ) .ver 4:0:0:0 }
.assembly 'prog' { .ver 0:0:0:0 }

.method public static int32 'sum'(native int, int32) cil managed
{
  .maxstack 4
  .locals (int32, int32)
  ldc.i4.0
  stloc.0
  ldarg.1
  ldc.i4.1
  blt @BB0_3
  ...
@BB0_3:
  ldloc.0
  ret
} // end of method 'sum'

// ---- undefined external functions: P/Invoke ----
.method public hidebysig static pinvokeimpl("ucrtbase" cdecl) int32 'puts'(native int) cil managed preservesig {}

// ---- data segment: 76 bytes (72 initialized + 4 zero), align 16 ----
.class private explicit ansi sealed '<msil>image_t' extends [mscorlib]System.ValueType
{
  .pack 1
  .size 72
}
.data cil '<msil>image_d' = bytearray (
  05 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 01 00 00 00   // 0x0000
  ... )
.field private static valuetype '<msil>image_t' '<msil>image' at '<msil>image_d'
.field private static initonly native int '<msil>data'
.field public static initonly native int 'table'        // +0
.field assembly static initonly native int '.L.str'     // +20

.method private hidebysig specialname rtspecialname static void .cctor() cil managed
{
  .maxstack 3
  ldc.i4 91
  conv.i
  call native int [mscorlib]System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal::AllocHGlobal(native int)
  ...                                                    // align, cpblk image, initblk bss,
  ret                                                    // address fields, relocations, ctors
} // end of method '.cctor'

.method private hidebysig static int32 '<msil>Main'(string[] args) cil managed
{
  .entrypoint
  .maxstack 4
  ...                                                    // argv from Environment::GetCommandLineArgs()
  call int32 'main'(int32, native int)
  ret
} // end of method '<msil>Main'
```

Rules (each verified by the recon experiments):
- Types: `int32` (class I32), `native int` (class I64, D2), `float32`, `float64`, `void`. Parameters are unnamed.
- Access: `public` for non-local linkage, `assembly` for internal/private (never `private`, never omitted).
- Instructions: one CIL opcode per line, two-space indent. Short forms are chosen by the printer: `ldarg.0-3`,
  `ldarg.s N` (N < 256), `ldarg N`; same for `ldloc`, `stloc`, `starg`; `ldc.i4.m1`, `ldc.i4.0-8`, `ldc.i4.s`
  (-128..127), `ldc.i4`. Branches always use the long forms (`br`, `brtrue`, `brfalse`, `beq`, `bne.un`, `blt`,
  `blt.un`, ...). FP constants are bit-exact: `ldc.r4 float32(0x7FC00000)`, `ldc.r8 float64(0x3FF8000000000000)`.
- Calls: `call int32 'f'(int32, native int)` (the same text as the callee's `.method` signature), `ldftn int32 'f'(int32)`,
  `calli int32(native int)` (managed in Phase 1).
- Globals: `ldsfld native int 'g'`, plus `ldc.i4 <off>` and `add` (or `ldc.i8 <off>; conv.i; add`) when the offset is
  non-zero.
- `switch (@BB0_1, @BB0_2)` is followed by `br @BB0_<default>`; the switch index is always int32 (a 64-bit value is
  range-checked first and converted with `conv.i4`, D35). Traps are `ldnull` + `throw`. Memory prefixes
  `unaligned. N` and `volatile.` are on their own lines before the opcode. Tees print `dup` + the store. A singlethread
  fence prints the comment `// MEMBARRIER`; other fences print
  `call void [mscorlib]System.Threading.Interlocked::MemoryBarrier()` (D36).
- Assembled with `ilasm -nologo -quiet -dll -pe64 -x64 -output=<x>.dll <x>.il`; run with
  `dotnet exec --runtimeconfig <net8 config> <x>.dll` from a private directory.

### 5.4 TableGen conventions and the opcode catalogue

- Single form (D1): `class MSILInst<bits<16> cilop, string asmstr>`; `NI<oops, iops, pattern, asmstr, cilop>`
  sets `Defs = [ARGUMENTS]`; `multiclass I` emits one `def ""`. Asm strings name only immediates and symbols.
- TSFlags: bits 1-0 `StackPeakExtra` (extra transient depth of multi-opcode records), bit 2 `TrapsOnlyOnUB`
  (div/rem: RegStackify may still move them). memflags immediate: bits 0-2 = unaligned N (0, 1, 2 or 4), bit 3 = volatile.
- Each `.td` area defines its own SDNodes (`-gen-sd-node-info` builds the `MSILISD` enum); `MSILISD::CALL` is C++-only.
- Register classes: `I32`, `I64` (FP, I64_0), `F32`, `F64`; fake regs `FP`, `VALUE_STACK`, `ARGUMENTS`;
  `defm : RemapAllTargetPseudoPointerOperands<I64>;`. In MIR the classes are `i32`, `i64`, `f32`, `f64` and the fake
  registers `$fp`, `$value_stack`, `$arguments`.
- Naming: `<MNEMONIC>_<class>`; conversions `CONV_<cil suffix>_<source class>`; `<RC>` below is I32, I64, F32, F64.

Operand definitions (M2.b; the PrintMethod names are what the generated `MSILGenAsmWriter.inc` calls on M2.c's
`MSILInstPrinter`, so they are a contract):

| Operand def | OperandType (`MSIL::`) | PrintMethod |
|---|---|---|
| `local_op` | `OPERAND_LOCAL` | `printLocalOperand` |
| `arg_op` | `OPERAND_ARG` | `printArgOperand` |
| `i32imm_op` | `OPERAND_I32IMM` | `printOperand` |
| `i64imm_op` | `OPERAND_I64IMM` | `printOperand` |
| `f32imm_op` | `OPERAND_F32IMM` | `printF32ImmOperand` |
| `f64imm_op` | `OPERAND_F64IMM` | `printF64ImmOperand` |
| `function_op` | `OPERAND_METHOD` | `printOperand` (a `MSILMemberRefExpr` after MCInstLower) |
| `data_op` | `OPERAND_DATA` | `printOperand` |
| `memflags_op` | `OPERAND_MEMFLAGS` | `printMemFlagsOperand` (prints the prefix lines) |
| `bb_op` (`Operand<OtherVT>`) | (none) | `printOperand` |

| Area (file, first milestone) | Records (CIL text; `+n` = StackPeakExtra) |
|---|---|
| Core (`MSILInstrInfo.td`, M2) | `ARGUMENT_<RC>` (none), `COPY_<RC>`, `TEE_<RC>`, `LOCAL_GET_<RC>` (ldloc), `LOCAL_SET_<RC>` (stloc), `LOCAL_TEE_<RC>` (dup; stloc, +1), `ARG_GET_<RC>` (ldarg), `ARG_SET_<RC>` (starg), `ARG_TEE_<RC>` (dup; starg, +1), `DROP_<RC>` (pop), `CONST_I32`, `CONST_I64` (ldc + conv.i), `CONST_F32`, `CONST_F64`, `GLOBAL_ADDR` (ldsfld [+ ldc.i4; add], +1), `FUNC_ADDR` (ldftn) |
| Control (`MSILInstrControl.td`, M2/M4/M6) | `RETURN` (ret), `TRAP` (ldnull; throw, +1), `BR`, `BR_IF` (brtrue), `BR_UNLESS` (brfalse), `BR_TABLE_I32` (switch (...); br; no I64 form, D35); M4: `SELECT_<RC>` (custom inserter, D34); M6: `B{EQ,NE_UN,LT,LT_UN,LE,LE_UN,GT,GT_UN,GE,GE_UN}_<RC>` |
| Calls (`MSILInstrCall.td`, M2/M4) | `ADJCALLSTACKDOWN`, `ADJCALLSTACKUP`, `CALL_PARAMS`, `CALL_RESULTS`, `CALL` (call <member-ref>), `CALL_INDIRECT` (calli <sig>) |
| Frame (`MSILInstrFrame.td`, M2) | `LOCALLOC` (localloc; never stackified, depth must be 1) |
| Integer (`MSILInstrInteger.td`, M4) | `ADD/SUB/MUL/AND/OR/XOR/SHL/SHR_S/SHR_U_{I32,I64}`, `DIV_S/DIV_U/REM_S/REM_U_{I32,I64}` (TrapsOnlyOnUB), `CEQ/CGT/CGT_UN/CLT/CLT_UN_{I32,I64}` (result I32) |
| Conversions (`MSILInstrConv.td`, M4/M5) | `CONV_I_I32` (conv.i), `CONV_U_I32` (conv.u), `CONV_I4_I64` (conv.i4), `CONV_I1_I32`, `CONV_I2_I32`, `CONV_U1_I32`, `CONV_U2_I32`; M5: `CONV_R4_{I32,I64,F64}`, `CONV_R8_{I32,I64,F32}`, `CONV_R_UN_I32`, `CONV_I4/U4/I/U_{F32,F64}` |
| FP (`MSILInstrFloat.td`, M5) | `ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/REM_{F32,F64}`, `NEG_{F32,F64}`, `CEQ/CGT/CGT_UN/CLT/CLT_UN_{F32,F64}` |
| Memory (`MSILInstrMemory.td`, M7) | `LDIND_{I1,U1,I2,U2,I4,I,R4,R8}`, `STIND_{I1,I2,I4,I,R4,R8}` (memflags first), `CPBLK`, `INITBLK`, `MEMMOVE` (conv.i8; dup; call Buffer::MemoryCopy, +1), `MEMORY_BARRIER` (call Interlocked::MemoryBarrier); singlethread fences select the generic `MEMBARRIER` (D36) |

Exact operand lists of the structural records (mirroring WebAssembly; MIR tests are written against this table, and no
later milestone may reorder it). Every record defined with `NI`/`I` also carries `implicit-def dead $arguments` in MIR.

| Record | `(outs)` | `(ins)` | Flags and notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ARGUMENT_<RC>` | `RC:$res` | `i32imm:$argno` | `Uses = [ARGUMENTS]`, `Defs = []`, hasSideEffects, isCodeGenOnly; MIR `%0:i32 = ARGUMENT_I32 0, implicit $arguments` |
| `COPY_<RC>` | `RC:$res` | `RC:$src` | isAsCheapAsAMove, isCodeGenOnly |
| `TEE_<RC>` | `RC:$res, RC:$also` | `RC:$src` | isAsCheapAsAMove, isCodeGenOnly |
| `LOCAL_GET_<RC>` | `RC:$res` | `local_op:$local` | mayLoad |
| `LOCAL_SET_<RC>` | - | `local_op:$local, RC:$src` | mayStore |
| `LOCAL_TEE_<RC>` | `RC:$res` | `local_op:$local, RC:$src` | mayStore, StackPeakExtra 1 |
| `ARG_GET_<RC>` | `RC:$res` | `arg_op:$arg` | mayLoad |
| `ARG_SET_<RC>` | - | `arg_op:$arg, RC:$src` | mayStore |
| `ARG_TEE_<RC>` | `RC:$res` | `arg_op:$arg, RC:$src` | mayStore, StackPeakExtra 1 |
| `DROP_<RC>` | - | `RC:$src` | |
| `CONST_I32` / `CONST_I64` | `I32:$res` / `I64:$res` | `i32imm_op:$imm` / `i64imm_op:$imm` | isMoveImm, isAsCheapAsAMove, isReMaterializable; patterns `imm` |
| `CONST_F32` / `CONST_F64` | `F32:$res` / `F64:$res` | `f32imm_op:$imm` / `f64imm_op:$imm` | as above; patterns `fpimm` |
| `GLOBAL_ADDR` | `I64:$res` | `data_op:$addr` | isReMaterializable, StackPeakExtra 1 (pattern in M8) |
| `FUNC_ADDR` | `I64:$res` | `function_op:$func` | isReMaterializable (pattern in M8) |
| `RETURN` | - | `variable_ops` | isReturn, isTerminator, isBarrier; MIR `RETURN %1, implicit-def dead $arguments` |
| `TRAP` | - | - | isTrap, isTerminator, isBarrier, hasCtrlDep; pattern `(trap)`; StackPeakExtra 1 |
| `BR` | - | `bb_op:$dst` | isBranch, isTerminator, isBarrier |
| `BR_IF` / `BR_UNLESS` | - | `bb_op:$dst, I32:$cond` | isBranch, isTerminator |
| `BR_TABLE_I32` | - | `I32:$index, variable_ops` | variable operands are MBBs, the last one is the default; isBranch, isTerminator, isBarrier |
| `SELECT_<RC>` (M4) | `RC:$dst` | `I32:$cond, RC:$t, RC:$f` | usesCustomInserter; pattern `(select I32:$cond, RC:$t, RC:$f)` |
| `ADJCALLSTACKDOWN` / `ADJCALLSTACKUP` | - | `i32imm:$amt, i32imm:$amt2` | isCodeGenOnly; callseq patterns |
| `CALL_PARAMS` | - | `function_op:$callee, variable_ops` | isCall; ISel only, recombined by the custom inserter |
| `CALL_RESULTS` | - | `variable_ops` | variadicOpsAreDefs, usesCustomInserter, isPseudo |
| `CALL` | - | `function_op:$callee, variable_ops` | variadicOpsAreDefs, isCall: defs first, then the callee (operand index = number of defs), then the argument uses |
| `CALL_INDIRECT` | - | `variable_ops` | variadicOpsAreDefs, isCall: defs first, then the argument uses, the callee address last (calli order); the signature is built by MCInstLower (M9) |
| `LOCALLOC` | `I64:$p` | `I32:$size` | hasSideEffects; never stackified; stack depth must be 1 when it executes |

Sample MIR (pre-ExplicitLocals, as a test WP writes it; register classes and operand order from the tables above):

```text
---
name:            f
tracksRegLiveness: true
machineFunctionInfo:
  params:  [ i32, i64 ]
  results: [ i32 ]
body: |
  bb.0:
    liveins: $arguments
    %0:i32 = ARGUMENT_I32 0, implicit $arguments
    %1:i64 = ARGUMENT_I64 1, implicit $arguments
    dead %2:i32 = CONST_I32 7, implicit-def dead $arguments
    RETURN %0, implicit-def dead $arguments
...
```

After `-run-pass=msil-explicit-locals` the use of `%0` reads `ARG_GET_I32 0`, the dead `CONST_I32` is followed by
`DROP_I32`, and non-argument values that are not stackified go through `LOCAL_SET_<RC>` / `LOCAL_GET_<RC>` with local
indices counted from 0 (passes-frame 7: unified numbering, params first, then CIL locals).

Stack effect contract (isel.md 9, passes-frame 8.2): after ExplicitLocals every explicit register use pops and every
explicit register def pushes (at most one), in operand order; `StackPeakExtra` covers multi-opcode records. Any record
that breaks this must be fixed, not special-cased in MSILStackCheck.

### 5.5 Test layout and harness conventions

| Tier | Location | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Triple / registry unit tests | `llvm/unittests/TargetParser/TripleTest.cpp`, `llvm/unittests/MC/TargetRegistry.cpp` | always built |
| Target unit tests | `llvm/unittests/Target/MSIL/` (`MSILTests`) | MSIL built |
| llc / MIR FileCheck | `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/` (`lit.local.cfg`: MSIL gate + optional `ilasm` feature + `%ilasm-verify`) | MSIL built |
| clang | `clang/test/CodeGen/MSIL/`, `clang/test/Preprocessor/init-msil.c`, `clang/test/Driver/msil-toolchain.c` | `REQUIRES: msil-registered-target` only when the backend runs |
| Execution | `msil/test/M1/<NN-area>/` (external project `msil/`) | `msil-exec` feature, else UNSUPPORTED |
| Harness self-tests | `msil/test/harness/` | ilasm + dotnet |

Execution directories: `00-smoke` (M3), `01-int` (M4), `02-fp` (M5), `03-control` (M6), `04-frames`, `05-memory` (M7),
`06-output`, `07-globals` (M8), `08-fnptr`, `09-structs`, `10-calls` (M9), `11-programs` (M10).

Execution-test rules:
- One RUN line, `%{msil_c}` (C) or `%{msil_ll}` (IR through llc), or a per-level form (`%{msil_c_O2}`) with a
  first-line comment saying why (D32). The first comment line says what the test covers.
- `.expected` is stdout (LF) plus `[exit N]` and is generated by `msil/utils/update-expected.py` from a native build.
- Tests are UB-free C11 that behaves identically at -O0 and -O2 natively. `main` always returns explicitly:
  `%{msil_cflags}` has `-Werror=return-type`, because `-ffreestanding` turns off main's implicit `return 0`.
- The exit status is 0..255 (D37): Linux truncates exit statuses to 8 bits, so a larger value that passes on Windows
  would pass on the WSL leg by accident. Bitmasks use at most 8 bits; programs return `checksum & 0xff`. msil-run.py
  and update-expected.py reject anything else.
- No `long`, `long double`, varargs, printing of addresses or floating-point printing; no libc beyond `puts` (through
  `msil/test/Inputs/msil_test.h`).

Capability rules. A test written before the capability it needs exists fails for the wrong reason, so tests (and
their RUN lines) respect these limits by milestone:

| Until | Not available | Write tests like this |
|---|---|---|
| M6 (control flow) | branches, loops, `switch`, `MSIL_EXPECT` (it is `if (!(c)) return ...`) | straight-line code and selects (M4); C tests accumulate with `MSIL_CHECK(acc, bit, cond)` and `return acc;` |
| M7 (frames, memory) | clang -O0 (every parameter and local becomes an alloca; windows-msvc gives even `main` a return-value slot), local arrays, address-taken locals, `fabs`/`copysign`/FP bitcasts (they go through a stack slot) | C at `%{msil_c_O2}` only (D32); produce -0.0 as `0.0 * -1.0`, NaN as `0.0 / 0.0`, test NaN with `fcmp uno` |
| M8 (globals, P/Invoke) | globals, string literals, brace- or string-initialized local arrays and structs (clang emits private `@__const` globals plus `llvm.memcpy`, even at -O0), output | results through the exit code only; initialize aggregates element by element |
| M9 (function pointers, aggregates) | indirect calls, `byval`/`sret` aggregates, K&R calls | direct calls with scalar arguments |

Each level runs compile -> `ilasm -dll` -> `msil-verify` -> `jitall` -> `dotnet exec` (private directory, timeout,
memory cap) -> transcript comparison. Every gate passes `msil_require_verify=1`, so a missing verifier or jitall is a
configuration error, not a silently skipped step (D38). The native-oracle (`msil_native_oracle`), .NET Framework
(`msil_run_netfx=1`), WSL (`msil_runner=wsl`, linux triple, .NET 10) and optimizing-JIT
(`msil_dotnet_env=DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0`) legs are parameters.

### 5.6 Phase 2 source layout and ownership

Phase 2 (M12-M23) creates the directories of 5.6.2 and changes the upstream files of 5.6.3. As in 5.2, every file has
exactly one owner per milestone. Owners are named as **roles** `M<n>/<role>`: a role is a set of files that one work
package owns. A milestone drafter may give several roles of one milestone to one WP, but never splits a role's files
across WPs, and never gives one file to two roles. Test roles (`*-tests`) are always separate WPs from the roles whose
code they test (section 1.4).

**Precedence.** Subsections 5.7 (ECMA-335 library), 5.8 (B2 objects and the link-info record) and 5.9 (msil-ld) own the
file names inside `llvm/include/llvm/CLI/`, `llvm/lib/CLI/`, `llvm/include/llvm/BinaryFormat/CLI*`,
`llvm/include/llvm/BinaryFormat/MSILLink.h`, `llvm/lib/MC/`, the MSIL target's MC/object-writer files and `lld/MSIL/`.
Where a name below differs from theirs, their name wins and the orchestrator corrects this table with a section 12 row;
the milestone and role assignment here stands. Sources: driver-toolchain 10, native-imports 8.1, bcl-binding 10,
lld-flavor 1.2/6.1, metadata-writer 4.1/7, mc-streamer 5.2/6, tests-p2 4, backlog 9, decision brief 2.

#### 5.6.1 Rules

1. **Fork prefixes.** M13 adds to `FORK_PREFIXES` of `msil/utils/ci/check-upstream-hooks.py`: `lld/MSIL/`,
   `lld/test/MSIL/`, `llvm/include/llvm/CLI/`, `llvm/lib/CLI/`, `llvm/unittests/CLI/`, `llvm/tools/llvm-cil-dump/`,
   `llvm/test/tools/llvm-cil-dump/`, `llvm/tools/llvm-cil-copy/`, `llvm/test/tools/llvm-cil-copy/`,
   `llvm/test/MC/MSIL/` (if M13 misses the two `llvm-cil-copy` prefixes, `M17/harness` adds them). Paths under a fork
   prefix need no manifest entry.
2. **Manifest duty.** A milestone that creates a fork file in an upstream directory adds a `fork-only <path>` line to
   `msil/utils/upstream-hooks.txt`; a milestone that edits an upstream file adds or updates its `hook <path>` block (at
   least one `lit`, `gtest`, `compile` or `none <reason>` line) and adjusts `min-pass`. The role that owns
   `msil/utils/upstream-hooks.txt` in that milestone (5.6.9) does it from the other roles' hand-overs. Every gate runs
   `upstream-hooks.ps1 -Leg manifest,pins` (5.12.10).
3. **Nothing downloaded or generated is committed**: corpus sources, reference packs, sysroots, WSL runtimes, built C#
   tools, lit outputs. They live under `C:\llvm-msil-scratch` (or `$HOME` inside WSL) and are found through lit
   parameters (5.12.2).
4. **Never edited by a WP:** `llvm/docs/MSIL/Design.md` (user), `llvm/docs/MSIL/ImplementationPlan.md` and
   `llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/**` (orchestrator), `llvm/docs/MSIL/FeatureIdeas.md` (end of the project only).
5. **Public repository.** No committed text contains a user-profile path, a user name or a session id. WSL paths are
   written with `$HOME`, Windows scratch paths as `C:\llvm-msil-scratch\...`.
6. **Retiring pinned text.** A milestone whose WPs change an msil-ld diagnostic, option or option set, the IL text that
   codegen or msil-ld prints (`-S`, llc, `--lto-emit-asm`), or the expansion of `%{msil_prog}`, `%{msil_c}`,
   `%{msil_ll}` or `%{msil_ldflags}` gives its test role the **whole** `lld/test/MSIL/` directory and its harness role
   the **whole** `msil/test/harness/prog/` directory (and `msil/test/harness/pipeline/` when the default `asm`
   expansions change). The WP description lists the earlier pinned texts the milestone retires (test file and old
   text), so the test author updates them from the specification. Known cases: 5.6.6 (`lld/test/MSIL/`) and 5.6.9
   (`msil/test/harness/prog/`); a milestone drafter who finds another applies the rule and notes it.
7. **Header first; no hand-over across a missing dependency.** The milestone workflow starts a WP only after every WP
   on its Depends-on line has finished. A header whose declarations a contract pins (5.9.2, 5.9.3, 5.11.5) and that
   another WP of the same milestone calls belongs to the role of a WP with no Depends-on line in that milestone (a
   root); its `.cpp` may stay with another role (5.6.6 applies this in M14, M20 and M21). An in-milestone check that
   uses another WP's file, script or private binary needs that WP on its Depends-on line; otherwise the check moves to
   the gate. Exception: a root test WP may syntax-check its files against same-milestone headers that already exist
   when it is ready to hand over; it never waits for, reads or builds them, and names the files it could not check as
   checked at the gate (5.7.14; M16.e, M16.f, M17.e).
8. **What a WP reads.** Phase 2 WPs read plan sections 1-4, the 5.x subsections their Reads line cites, their own
   milestone and its section 12 rows, not all of sections 1-6 (the orchestrator records this as a section 12 row
   amending 1.1 and uses the same wording in the workflow's prompts). A Reads line cites 5.7.10 for every test that
   FileChecks `llvm-cil-dump` or `mdcanon` output (and 5.8.11 when it checks `--link-info`), 5.9.14, 5.10.14 or 5.11.9
   for every test of msil-ld diagnostics, and 5.12.1-5.12.6 for every harness or execution test. A test WP never reads a
   file that a non-test WP of its milestone owns (infra and docs included): it reads the committed state with
   `git show HEAD:<path>` and the plan text (for example plan D14, not Status.md).

#### 5.6.10 The M13 batch and its measured rebuild cost

Every upstream hook and every widely-included or shared header Phase 2 needs lands in M13 (the M1 of Phase 2), so
M14-M23 rebuild only new libraries, the MSIL target, clang driver TUs and lld. Measured on 2026-10-21 from the shared
build's `.ninja_deps` (3,218 objects) and `.ninja_log` (3.17 CPU-hours of compile = the 47-minute full rebuild), read
only; Attr.td variants were run through the tree's `clang-tblgen` into scratch with `--write-if-changed` semantics
compared (scripts in `C:\llvm-msil-scratch\p2-plan\tooling\`):

| M13 edit | What rebuilds | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `Attr.td`: new `TargetWebAssemblyOrMSIL` and the two import records retargeted to it (5.10.7) | of the 22 generated `.inc` files only `AttrHasAttributeImpl.inc` (1 object) and `AttrParsedAttrImpl.inc` (3 objects) change | ~95 CPU-s (`ParsedAttr.cpp` 21 s) |
| `AttrDocs.td` text | `AttrDocTable.inc` (`AttrDocTable.cpp`) | 2 s |
| for contrast: a new attribute record or a shared `ParseKind` (backlog 2.5 (a)/(b)) | `Attrs.inc`/`AttrParsedAttrList.inc`: 519-523 objects | 3,500 CPU-s, 31%, ~8.4 min: **not used** |
| `DiagnosticDriverKinds.td`: one reworded and one new error, no new group | `DiagnosticDriverKinds.inc`: 84 objects | 282 CPU-s (2.5%), ~0.7 min |
| `CodeGenModule.cpp`, `ParsePragma.cpp` | 1 object each | 25 s, 16.5 s |
| `IRSymtab.cpp`, `Triple.cpp` (+ `TripleTest.cpp`) | 1 object each | 1.9 s, 2.8 s (+16.9 s) |
| `MCContext.cpp`, `TargetRegistry.cpp`, `MCAsmBackend.cpp` | 3 objects | 8.6 s |
| new headers (`BinaryFormat/CLI.h`, `CLITables.def`, `CILOpcodes.def`, `MSILLink.h`, `MC/MCSymbolMSIL.h`, `MCMSILStreamer.h`, `MCMSILObjectWriter.h`) | no existing dependents | 0 |
| relinks | `clang.exe` 7.2 s, `opt.exe` 3.8 s, `llc.exe` 2.2 s, `MSILTests` 1.1 s, `MCTests` 1.0 s, `TargetParserTests` 0.3 s | ~20 s |
| CMake lists (`llvm/lib`, `llvm/unittests`, `llvm/lib/MC`, lld) | one CMake regeneration | not measured (minutes) |
| new: `lld` (126 compiles, 5 LLVM TUs, 7 TableGen runs, lld-flavor 5) | first build | 2.5-3 min wall at -j4 |
| new: `llvm-ar` and its three copies, `llvm-nm`, `llvm-objdump`, `llvm-readobj` (5 + 3 + 11 + 13 TUs), `llvm-as`, `llvm-bcanalyzer`, `llvm-lto2`, `CLITests` skeleton, `LLDAsLibAllTests` | first build | ~2-4 min (estimate: mostly links) |

**Result: M13 is not a clang-wide rebuild.** The hooks compile in about 1.5-2 minutes of wall time; with the new tools
and the regeneration the M13 build is about 8-12 minutes. Q35's spelling holds; only the brief's rebuild estimate
changes (open question 1).

#### 5.6.11 Build targets per milestone, and disk on D:

There is **one** list. It only grows, and every milestone builds all of it, so no gate runs a stale binary (a stale
`LLDAsLibAllTests` or `llvm-lto2` would test an old lldMSIL or LTO in the upstream-hooks legs of M14 and M19):

| Milestones | The complete build-target list (in this order) |
|---|---|
| M12 | the M11 set: `llc opt clang FileCheck not count split-file llvm-config llvm-profdata TargetParserTests MCTests MSILTests` |
| M13, M14 | the M11 set, then `lld llvm-ar llvm-ranlib llvm-lib llvm-dlltool llvm-nm llvm-objdump llvm-readobj llvm-as llvm-bcanalyzer llvm-lto2 CLITests LLDAsLibAllTests` |
| M15, M16 | the M13 list, then `yaml2obj llvm-mc` (versioned `.so` inputs, native-imports 9.1) |
| M17-M23 | the M15 list, then `llvm-cil-dump llvm-cil-copy` |

Why each M13 target: `lld` builds `lld.exe` and its copies `msil-ld`, `ld.lld`, `lld-link`, `ld64.lld` and `wasm-ld`
(`add_lld_symlink` passes `ALWAYS_GENERATE`). `llvm-ranlib`, `llvm-lib` and `llvm-dlltool` are **not** built by
`ninja llvm-ar`: `llvm/tools/llvm-ar/CMakeLists.txt:22-24` calls `add_llvm_tool_symlink` without `ALWAYS_GENERATE`, so
each copy is its own custom target (`AddLLVM.cmake`, `build llvm-lib: phony tools/llvm-ar/llvm-lib`). Without them
`llvm-lib /def:` in lld/test/MSIL (M14, M15) silently resolves to the VS 22.x `llvm-lib` on msil-env's PATH, and the
Linux CI job has none. `llvm-as` and `llvm-bcanalyzer` serve the `IRSymtab.cpp` hook's upstream tests, `llvm-lto2` its
`LTO/Resolution/X86/symtab*.ll` tests, `LLDAsLibAllTests` the `AllDrivers.cpp` hook (D9 row of section 12).

**One source.** `M13/infra` writes the list to `msil/utils/ci/build-targets.txt` (one target per line, `#` comments
allowed), makes `build.ps1` and `build.sh` read it, and gives `msil/utils/build/msil-build.ps1` the switch `-Standard`
(build every target of that file, then any target named on the command line; `$Targets` is no longer mandatory with
`-Standard`). `M15/harness` and `M17/harness` append their targets to the file. From M13 on, gate step G1 is
`msil-build.ps1 -Standard`; each milestone's **Build targets** line spells out its row of the table above, and the
role that edits `build-targets.txt` checks the file against that row.

Never `check-lld`, `check-llvm`, `check-clang` or `check-all` (lld-flavor 5). Disk: the lld copies cost about 0.4 GB;
the three `llvm-ar` copies, `llvm-lto2`, `LLDAsLibAllTests` and the other new tools about 1.0-1.5 GB (estimate from
the sizes of `llc.exe`/`opt.exe`, 59 MB each); D: had 21-23 GB free on 2026-10-21. Every Phase 2 gate prints D:'s
free space first; below 8 GB the orchestrator reports it to the user before building.

### 5.7 ECMA-335 library (llvm/lib/CLI)

One library reads and writes ECMA-335 modules for every Phase-2 consumer (decision Q28): the MSIL target (binary CIL
encoding and synthesized bodies from M18, netmodule objects from M19), msil-ld (object input, the output PE, reference
binding, P2-C inputs; M20-M22) and the tools `llvm-cil-dump` and `llvm-cil-copy`. Format constants live in
`llvm/include/llvm/BinaryFormat/CLI.h` with two X-macro files; everything else is the LLVM component `CLI`
(`LLVMCLI`), namespace `llvm::cli`. It lands in three milestones:

- **M13**: format headers, handles, the table schema, the CMake hooks and the `CLITests` skeleton.
- **M16** (writer half): blobs, signatures, custom attributes; opcodes, IL builder, IL decoder, method bodies; heaps
  and `MetadataBuilder`; the C# oracle tools `mdump` and `mdcanon`.
- **M17**: PE writer, PE image and metadata reader, dumper, `llvm-cil-dump`, `llvm-cil-copy`, and the codecs of the
  link-info record and the P2-C symbol-table attribute.

Later milestones add files that other contracts specify, as 5.7.1's table lists: the public BCL member list
`BCLMembers.{def,h}` in M18 (5.7.2, content 5.11.7) and the link model's `ImageLayout`, `Trailer` and `CallAdapter` in
M20 (5.9.8-5.9.10). M20-M22 extend `BCLMembers.def` and `Trailer`, and M22 extends the symbol-table codec.

Sources: metadata-writer 4-7 (its prototype `metadata-writer-files/py/cliwriter.py` is an executable specification:
when it and the C++ library disagree on the same input, one of them has a bug), bcl-binding 5.2-5.7 and 7,
mc-streamer 5.3-5.5 and 5.10, objfmt-binding 3 and 11, lld-flavor 4, exports-multiasm 5 and 10.4, tests-p2 3.7-3.9,
judge-dotnet-value 5.7 and 7.3. Every name below is a contract (section 1.9). A WP that needs a different name or
signature stops and reports it; the orchestrator records the change in section 12 before the milestone commit.

**Reading this section.** It is about 100 KB, so a Reads line cites subsections of 5.7, never "5.7" or "this section"
as a whole. The rules:
- a WP that writes files under `llvm/include/llvm/CLI/`, `llvm/lib/CLI/` or `llvm/unittests/CLI/` cites 5.7.1
  (layout, CMake, conventions) and 5.7.12 (errors, determinism, limits), plus the subsections of the headers it
  writes or tests;
- a consumer cites the subsections of the headers it calls (5.7.15 lists them per milestone);
- a test that FileChecks `llvm-cil-dump` or `%msil_canon` output cites 5.7.10, and also 5.8.11 when it checks
  `--link-info`.

#### 5.7.1 Layout, CMake and dependencies

| Path | Contents | Lands |
|---|---|---|
| `llvm/include/llvm/BinaryFormat/CLI.h` | constants, enums, tokens, compressed integers, on-disk headers, limits (5.7.2); header-only | M13 |

| `llvm/include/llvm/BinaryFormat/CILOpcodes.def` | ECMA-335 III opcodes (5.7.2) | M13 |

| `llvm/include/llvm/CLI/{ImageLayout,Trailer,CallAdapter}.h`, `llvm/lib/CLI/{ImageLayout,Trailer,CallAdapter}.cpp` | the link contract's lib/CLI files (5.9.8-5.9.10) | M20 (`Trailer.*` extended in M21 and M22) |
| `llvm/lib/CLI/CMakeLists.txt` | the component | M13 (created), M16, M17 and M20 (extended) |
| `llvm/tools/llvm-cil-dump/{CMakeLists.txt,llvm-cil-dump.cpp}`, `llvm/tools/llvm-cil-copy/{CMakeLists.txt,llvm-cil-copy.cpp}` | 5.7.10 | M17 |

Rules:
- **CMake.** `add_llvm_component_library(LLVMCLI <sources> ADDITIONAL_HEADER_DIRS ${LLVM_MAIN_INCLUDE_DIR}/llvm/CLI
  LINK_COMPONENTS BinaryFormat MC Support TargetParser)`. MC is only for `StringTableBuilder` (the `#Strings` heap),
  and TargetParser only for `PEOptions::get(const Triple &, ...)`. There is **no `Object` dependency**: PE headers
  are written and parsed with `support::endian` and the constants of `BinaryFormat/COFF.h`. The unit tests use
  `add_llvm_unittest(CLITests ...)` with `LLVM_LINK_COMPONENTS CLI Support TargetParser` and `LLVMTestingSupport`
  (from M13: `MSILLinkTest.cpp` builds `Triple`s for `MSILLink::setDataModel`, and LLVM lists the components a target
  uses directly).
- **Upstream-file edits.** Exactly two one-line `add_subdirectory(CLI)` edits:
  - `llvm/lib/CMakeLists.txt`, after `add_subdirectory(Object)` (line 31);
  - `llvm/unittests/CMakeLists.txt`, between `add_subdirectory(CGData)` and `add_subdirectory(CodeGen)` (lines 39-40).

  The tools need no hook, because `add_llvm_implicit_projects` picks them up. The upstream-hooks check (M11.d) must
  know about all of this in M13. The M13 WP that owns `msil/utils/upstream-hooks.txt` and
  `msil/utils/ci/check-upstream-hooks.py` (5.6) adds:
  - `hook` blocks for the two CMake files, each with `none build wiring of the fork's llvm/lib/CLI; built and run by
    the CLITests gate step`;
  - `fork-only` lines for the four BinaryFormat files (`CLI.h`, `CLITables.def`, `CILOpcodes.def` and 5.8's
    `MSILLink.h`);
  - the new directories `llvm/include/llvm/CLI/`, `llvm/lib/CLI/`, `llvm/unittests/CLI/`, `llvm/tools/llvm-cil-dump/`,
    `llvm/tools/llvm-cil-copy/`, `llvm/test/tools/llvm-cil-dump/` and `llvm/test/tools/llvm-cil-copy/` in
    `FORK_PREFIXES`.
- **Who links the library.** Consumers link `CLI` through `LINK_COMPONENTS`:
  - `MSILDesc` and `MSILCodeGen` from M18;
  - `lldMSIL` from M20 (M14 and M15 do not need it);
  - the two tools and `CLITests`.

  `LLVMMC` never depends on `LLVMCLI`, which depends on `LLVMMC`. `MCSymbolMSIL.h` may name `cli::MethodSig` only
  through a forward declaration (`namespace llvm::cli { struct MethodSig; }`), and no lib/MC `.cpp` calls an LLVMCLI
  function.
- **Conventions** (section 2):
  - the LLVM banner, and `LLVM_ABI` on every exported declaration under `llvm/include/llvm/CLI/`;
  - header guards `LLVM_BINARYFORMAT_CLI_H` and `LLVM_CLI_<FILE>_H`; `DEBUG_TYPE "cli-<file>"`; no `cl::opt` in the
    library;
  - **one namespace `llvm::cli`, BinaryFormat constants included.** There is no `llvm::CLI`, because two namespaces
    that differ only in case read as one.
- **Checking work before the gate.** Until the gate's configure step knows lib/CLI, implementers syntax-check with
  `msil-syntax.ps1 -FlagsFrom llvm/lib/MC/StringTableBuilder.cpp <files>`. They may also compile and link private
  copies of `LLVMCLI` and its tests under `C:\llvm-msil-scratch\` against the shared build's `.lib` files (as M11.a
  did for llc), never in `D:\llvm-msil\build`. A private build serves only the WP that made it. It compiles only
  the WP's own sources and sources that were complete when the WP started (earlier milestones and the WPs it
  depends on, 5.7.14). No
  WP's check uses a binary that another WP of the same milestone built. Test WPs run only binaries that already exist
  in the shared build or in the oracle tools of earlier milestones; this milestone's `CLITests`, `llvm-cil-dump`
  and `llvm-cil-copy` first run for them at the gate. M13, M16, M17 and M20 add lib/CLI sources or tools, so each of
  their gates runs `msil-configure.ps1` first.

#### 5.7.2 BinaryFormat/CLI.h, the .def files and Handles.h (M13); BCLMembers (M18)

Start from the verified drafts `llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/metadata-writer-files/CLITables.def` and `CILOpcodes.def`.
Add the LLVM banner, replace the draft comments, and keep the entries and their order. The macro contracts:

```cpp
// CLITables.def: three independent sections; each is expanded only if its macro is defined and #undef's it.
CLI_TABLE(Id, Name, Sorted)                // Id 0x00..0x2C, Name as in ECMA II.22, Sorted 0/1 (II.22 sort order)
CLI_COLUMN(Table, Column, Kind, Target)    // ECMA column order. Kind: U16 U32 StringIdx GuidIdx BlobIdx TableIdx
                                           // CodedIdx. Target: a table (TableIdx), a coded index (CodedIdx) or None
CLI_CODED_INDEX(Name, TagBits, Tables...)  // tables in tag order; None marks an unused tag
// CILOpcodes.def: #error unless CIL_OPCODE is defined; #undef at the end. 219 entries in value order: the 218
// opcodes of System.Reflection.Emit.OpCodes plus ECMA's no. (0xFE19).
CIL_OPCODE(Enum, Text, Value, Operand, Pop, Push, Flow) // Value 0x00XX or 0xFEXX; Operand an OperandKind; Pop and
                                           // Push StackBehaviour names; Flow a FlowControl name
```

`CLI.h`, namespace `llvm::cli`:

```cpp
enum class TableId : uint8_t { /* CLI_TABLE: Module = 0x00, TypeRef = 0x01, ..., GenericParamConstraint = 0x2C */ };
// 0x30-0x37 (Portable PDB, Phase 4) are reserved: no enumerators and no schema in Phase 2.
constexpr unsigned NumTableIds = 64;            // width of the #~ Valid and Sorted vectors
enum class CodedIndexKind : uint8_t { /* CLI_CODED_INDEX order: TypeDefOrRef, ..., TypeOrMethodDef */ };
enum class ColumnKind : uint8_t { U16, U32, StringIdx, GuidIdx, BlobIdx, TableIdx, CodedIdx };

constexpr uint32_t makeToken(TableId T, uint32_t Row);   // (T << 24) | Row, Row < 2^24
constexpr uint8_t getTokenType(uint32_t Token);          // high byte: a TableId value, or 0x70
constexpr uint32_t getTokenRow(uint32_t Token);          // low 24 bits
constexpr uint8_t UserStringTokenType = 0x70;            // ldstr operand: 0x70000000 | #US offset

enum class OperandKind : uint8_t { InlineNone, ShortInlineVar, InlineVar, ShortInlineI, InlineI, InlineI8,
  ShortInlineR, InlineR, ShortInlineBrTarget, InlineBrTarget, InlineMethod, InlineField, InlineType, InlineTok,
  InlineSig, InlineString, InlineSwitch };
enum class StackBehaviour : uint8_t { /* one enumerator for each Pop and Push name CILOpcodes.def uses, spelled as in
  System.Reflection.Emit.StackBehaviour: Pop0, Pop1, Pop1_pop1, Popi, ..., Push0, ..., Varpop, Varpush */ };
enum class FlowControl : uint8_t { Branch, Break, Call, Cond_Branch, Meta, Next, Return, Throw };
enum class Opcode : uint16_t { /* CIL_OPCODE: Nop = 0x0000, ..., Ldc_i4_s = 0x001F, ..., Readonly = 0xFE1E */ };
constexpr uint8_t TwoByteOpcodePrefix = 0xFE;

enum ElementType : uint8_t { ELEMENT_TYPE_END = 0x00, ELEMENT_TYPE_VOID = 0x01, /* every II.23.1.16 value
  through */ ELEMENT_TYPE_CMOD_REQD = 0x1F, ELEMENT_TYPE_CMOD_OPT = 0x20, ELEMENT_TYPE_INTERNAL = 0x21,
  ELEMENT_TYPE_MODIFIER = 0x40, ELEMENT_TYPE_SENTINEL = 0x41, ELEMENT_TYPE_PINNED = 0x45 };
enum SerializationTypeCode : uint8_t { SERIALIZATION_TYPE_TYPE = 0x50, SERIALIZATION_TYPE_TAGGED_OBJECT = 0x51,
  SERIALIZATION_TYPE_FIELD = 0x53, SERIALIZATION_TYPE_PROPERTY = 0x54, SERIALIZATION_TYPE_ENUM = 0x55 };
enum SignatureHeader : uint8_t { SIG_DEFAULT = 0x00, SIG_C = 0x01, SIG_STDCALL = 0x02, SIG_THISCALL = 0x03,
  SIG_FASTCALL = 0x04, SIG_VARARG = 0x05, SIG_FIELD = 0x06, SIG_LOCAL = 0x07, SIG_PROPERTY = 0x08,
  SIG_UNMANAGED = 0x09, SIG_GENERICINST = 0x0A, SIG_KIND_MASK = 0x0F, SIG_GENERIC = 0x10, SIG_HASTHIS = 0x20,
  SIG_EXPLICITTHIS = 0x40 };
```

- **Attribute flag enums.** Scoped, marked with `LLVM_MARK_AS_BITMASK_ENUM`, and containing every value of ECMA
  II.23.1:
  - `TypeAttributes : uint32_t`, `FieldAttributes : uint16_t`, `MethodAttributes : uint16_t`,
    `MethodImplAttributes : uint16_t`, `ParamAttributes : uint16_t`, `PropertyAttributes : uint16_t`,
    `MethodSemanticsAttributes : uint16_t`, `PInvokeAttributes : uint16_t`, `GenericParamAttributes : uint16_t`,
    `AssemblyFlags : uint32_t`, `ManifestResourceAttributes : uint32_t`, `FileAttributes : uint32_t`;
  - `AssemblyHashAlgorithm : uint32_t` (`None = 0`, `MD5 = 0x8003`, `SHA1 = 0x8004`).

  Enumerators carry the ECMA flag names in UpperCamelCase, as System.Reflection spells them. Examples:
  `TypeAttributes::Public`, `TypeAttributes::BeforeFieldInit`, `TypeAttributes::Forwarder` (0x00200000),
  `MethodAttributes::PrivateScope`, `MethodAttributes::HideBySig`, `MethodAttributes::SpecialName`,
