**Exit criteria**
- llc and clang -S produce assemblable IL for leaf functions; 00-smoke passes (llc -O0/-O2 for the .ll tests, clang -O2 for the C tests) on .NET 8 (Windows) and .NET 10 (WSL, linux triple).
- jitall and msil-verify (enforced, msil_require_verify=1) pass for every 00-smoke DLL.
- MIR tests prove ARG/LOCAL numbering, the LOCALLOC root rule and every MSILStackCheck failure mode.
- No 'not a recognized processor/feature' warnings for clang-produced attributes; clang -S works for the MinGW triple.
- Copied passes keep the D30 header and differ from WebAssembly only by the listed changes.

**Review focus** (in addition to the three standing lenses)
- CIL correctness: exact .maxstack, ldarg/starg vs ldloc/stloc split, no falling off a method, entry point argv building.
- Diff hygiene of copied passes vs WebAssembly (mechanical renames only plus listed MSIL rules).
- Signature consistency between definition headers and MFI (assertion present), widened param types (narrow-param hazard).
- Tests cover boundaries (short forms), quoting, negative MIR cases; execution on both triples.

**Rebuild cost.** MSIL target TUs only (~20 changed) + relink llc/opt/clang/MSILTests: ~5-15 min.

### M4. Direct calls, integer arithmetic and select

**Goal.** Direct calls with scalar signatures (narrow integers widened to int32, 64-bit values as native int), every integer ALU operation, integer comparisons as values, integer width conversions, SELECT through a branch triangle (D34; generic legalization emits SELECT for variable i128 shifts and min/max), and i128 arithmetic expanded inline (no runtime helpers). Diagnosed calls (variadic, runtime library, mismatched signature) end in exit code 1 without a crash. llc -O2 programs made of noinline helper calls and selects run correctly.

**Depends on:** M3.

**Header changes:**
- none

**Work packages**

#### M4.a Direct calls: LowerCall, CALL split, call results inserter, call-site lowering (implement, ~800 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrCall.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLoweringCall.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelDAGToDAG.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILMCInstLower.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILMCInstLower.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md sections 2.4-2.5, 8, 11.1, 11.5; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/asmprinter.md section 6.4; llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssemblyISelLowering.cpp (LowerCall), WebAssemblyISelDAGToDAG.cpp (CALL split), WebAssemblyMCInstLower.cpp
- Provides: MSILTargetLowering::emitCallResults(MachineInstr&, MachineBasicBlock*) (called by the EmitInstrWithCustomInserter dispatch in M4.b)
- Consumes: MSILAsmPrinter::getSignature / noteExternFunction (M2.d API, made usable by M4.c); MSILISD::CALL (M2.f); MSILMemberRefExpr::createMethod (M2.c)

Copy WebAssembly's LowerCall (isel.md 11.1) without tail calls (IsTailCall = false), Swift, funcref/table or Emscripten paths: build MSILISD::CALL (chain, callee, args...) with TargetGlobalAddress / TargetExternalSymbol callees; variadic calls -> DiagnosticInfoUnsupported 'calls to variadic functions are not supported for MSIL yet' (M9 fixes K&R-typed calls to defined functions before ISel); byval args -> diagnostic (M9); an ExternalSymbol callee -> DiagnosticInfoUnsupported "runtime library call '<name>' is not supported for MSIL yet" (M8 replaces this policy); a direct call whose call-site FunctionType differs from the callee's -> DiagnosticInfoUnsupported 'mismatched call signature' (backstop until FixFunctionBitcasts, M9). After any of these diagnostics LowerCall builds no call node: it returns CLI.Chain and pushes DAG.getUNDEF(In.VT) for every entry of CLI.Ins (section 2 diagnostics rule; the same pattern M7 uses for dynamic alloca), so ISel, the custom inserter and MCInstLower never meet the callee and llc exits 1 without a stack dump. DAGToDAG: split MSILISD::CALL into CALL_PARAMS/CALL_RESULTS exactly as WebAssembly (strip the FUNC_ADDR/EXT_SYM wrappers for direct callees). emitCallResults (custom inserter) recombines into CALL (direct; callee operand index = number of defs) or CALL_INDIRECT (callee moved last; completed in M9). MSILInstrCall.td: callseq patterns and any operand fixes. MSILMCInstLower: MO_GlobalAddress of a Function -> MSILMemberRefExpr::createMethod(getILName(F), &Printer.getSignature(F), Ctx) and Printer.noteExternFunction(F) for declarations; non-function GlobalAddress and ExternalSymbol stay fatal until M8.

#### M4.b Integer ISel, select triangles and legalization (implement, ~1050 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrInteger.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrConv.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILSubtarget.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILSubtarget.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrControl.td`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/wasm-inventory.md sections 3.6.2, 3.6.4 (integer rows), 3.7; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md sections 3.1, 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 6, 7.1, 10.5; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md section 11.6 (select triangle)
- Provides: integer opcode names of plan 5.4 (ADD_I32 ... CLT_UN_I64, CONV_I_I32, CONV_U_I32, CONV_I4_I64, CONV_I1_I32, CONV_I2_I32, CONV_U1_I32, CONV_U2_I32); SELECT_I32, SELECT_I64, SELECT_F32, SELECT_F64 ((outs RC:$dst) (ins I32:$cond, RC:$t, RC:$f), usesCustomInserter); MSILTargetLowering::emitSelect
- Consumes: emitCallResults (M4.a)

Records and patterns (single form): ADD/SUB/MUL/AND/OR/XOR/SHL/SHR_S/SHR_U and DIV_S/DIV_U/REM_S/REM_U for I32 and I64 (DIV/REM: hasSideEffects = 1, TrapsOnlyOnUB = 1); shift amounts are I32 for both widths (getScalarShiftAmountTy is i32); keep LLVM's shift masks (never port wasm's mask-stripping patterns); NEG/NOT optional; compares CEQ/CGT/CGT_UN/CLT/CLT_UN for I32 and I64 producing I32, with the negated predicates built from single-opcode MIs at ISel (setne -> CEQ(CEQ(a,b), CONST_I32 0); setle -> CEQ(CGT(a,b),0); and so on, isel.md decision 2); integer conversions in MSILInstrConv.td (integer part only): sext i32->i64 conv.i, zext/anyext conv.u, trunc i64->i32 conv.i4, sext_inreg i8/i16 conv.i1/conv.i2 (I32) and the I64 forms per isel.md 5.4. setOperationAction per isel.md 6 integer rows: i1/i8/i16 promoted; CTLZ/CTTZ/CTPOP/BSWAP/ROTL/ROTR Expand (no BCL intrinsics, decision D16); MULHS/MULHU/SMUL_LOHI/UMUL_LOHI/SDIVREM/UDIVREM Expand; SHL_PARTS/SRA_PARTS/SRL_PARTS Custom via expandShiftParts (LowerShiftParts); SELECT_CC/BR_CC Expand; SETCC Legal for i32/i64; SELECT Legal for i32/i64/f32/f64 through new pseudos in MSILInstrControl.td: SELECT_{I32,I64,F32,F64} with (outs RC:$dst) (ins I32:$cond, RC:$t, RC:$f), pattern (select I32:$cond, RC:$t, RC:$f), usesCustomInserter = 1 (decision D34). emitSelect (isel.md 11.6) splits the block into a triangle: ThisMBB ends with 'BR_IF SinkMBB, $cond' (the taken edge carries $t), an empty FalseMBB falls through to SinkMBB carrying $f, and SinkMBB starts with '$dst = PHI $t, ThisMBB, $f, FalseMBB'; successor lists and the PHI are built explicitly (analyzeBranch still returns true until M6, so nothing may rely on branch analysis). BR_IF and bb_op exist since M2.b, MCInstLower lowers MBB operands since M2.d, and M4.c prints branches and labels. Generic code needs SELECT from here on: expandShiftParts for variable-amount i128 shifts (TargetLowering.cpp ~9449-9457), the SMIN/SMAX/UMIN/UMAX expansions and min/max idioms; convertSelectOfConstantsToMath is true since M2.f, so sext/zext of a compare stays arithmetic. EmitInstrWithCustomInserter dispatches MSIL::CALL_RESULTS to emitCallResults and SELECT_* to emitSelect. MSILSubtarget::initLibcallLoweringInfo marks MUL_I128, MULO_I64 and MULO_I128 unsupported so they expand inline (isel decision 10; confirm the LibcallLoweringInfo API at HEAD).

#### M4.c Call-site printing and signature services (implement, ~300 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILAsmPrinter.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILAsmPrinter.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MCTargetDesc/MSILInstPrinter.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MCTargetDesc/MSILInstPrinter.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/asmprinter.md sections 5.3, 6.3-6.4; this plan section 5.1

Make the M2 signature services production quality: getSignature for declarations and definitions alike, noteExternFunction collecting undefined callees; at emitEndOfAsmFile, if ExternFuncs is non-empty, emit the error "call to external function '<name>' needs P/Invoke support (M8)" (temporary, replaced in M8). InstPrinter: CALL prints 'call <member-ref>' (operand index = number of defs because of variadicOpsAreDefs), CALL_INDIRECT prints 'calli <sig>' (M9 supplies the operand); verify every integer record prints the plan 5.4 mnemonic. Branch printing lands here because select triangles produce the first branches (D34): BR prints 'br <label>', BR_IF 'brtrue <label>', BR_UNLESS 'brfalse <label>', always the long forms; MBB operands print as '@BB<f>_<b>' and the base AsmPrinter's block labels as '@BB<f>_<b>:' (InternalSymbolPrefix '@'); block comments use '//'.

#### M4.e Execution tests for calls and integers (test, ~600 lines)

- Owned files: `msil/test/M1/01-int/`
- Reads: this plan section 5.5 and decisions D32, D34, D37; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/tests-ci.md sections 6.4, 7.1

Straight-line programs plus selects (no branches until M6) with noinline helpers so llc -O2 cannot fold: add-args.ll, int32-ops.ll and int64-ops.ll (each check sets one bit of an 8-bit mask that is returned as the exit code; never more than 8 bits, D37), narrow-ints.ll (signext/zeroext), i128-ops.ll (mul, shifts by constant and by variable amounts, add with carry), select-values.ll (selects of every value type on integer conditions, incl. signed/unsigned min and max), many-args.ll (12 mixed i32/i64 args), call-chain.ll, div-rem.ll (in-range values only; INT_MIN/-1 is UB). **Exit criteria**
- Direct calls, every integer operation and selects compile, assemble, verify and run; 01-int passes on .NET 8 and on WSL .NET 10.
- i128 add/sub/mul and constant and variable shifts never reference a runtime helper.
- Unsupported calls fail with clear diagnostics, exit code 1 and no crash marker.
- sext/zext of a compare stays arithmetic; every select is a brtrue triangle; branches print in long form with '@BB' labels.
- Call-site tokens always equal the callee's method signature.

**Review focus** (in addition to the three standing lenses)
- CIL semantics: sign/zero extension at int32/native int boundaries, shift amount typing, negated compares, div/rem side effects.
- WebAssembly call machinery copied faithfully (CALL_PARAMS/CALL_RESULTS); diagnostics instead of crashes.
- No int64 typing anywhere (decision D2); PEVerify clean except allow-listed codes.
- Test adequacy: boundary values, both triples, -O0/-O2 where possible.
- emitSelect builds correct successor lists and PHIs without relying on analyzeBranch; -verify-machineinstrs clean.

**Rebuild cost.** MSIL target TUs + relink: ~5-15 min.

### M5. Floating point and conversions

**Goal.** f32/f64 arithmetic, FP comparisons as values with exact NaN semantics, int<->fp conversions with correctly rounded uint64->fp on every runtime through a select-free, memory-free sequence (D17), frem and fneg; FP operations that become library calls are diagnosed until M8, and fabs/copysign/bitcasts (through memory) wait for M7. update_llc_test_checks.py learns MSIL.

**Depends on:** M4.

**Header changes:**
- none

**Work packages**

#### M5.a FP and conversion ISel (implement, ~700 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrFloat.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrConv.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/wasm-inventory.md sections 3.6.3-3.6.4; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md sections 3.2, 5.2, 5.4, 5.6, 6 (FP rows); llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/cil-runtime.md (e05, e05b conversions); llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG/LegalizeDAG.cpp (ExpandLegalINT_TO_FP ~2880-2935) and TargetLowering.cpp (expandUINT_TO_FP ~10340-10383); this plan decisions D16, D17
- Provides: `FP opcode names of plan 5.4 (ADD_F32 ... CONV_U_F64); there is no CONV_R_UN_I64 (D17)`

ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/REM for F32 and F64 (FREM Legal -> CIL rem, verified equal to fmod), NEG_F32/F64 (fneg -> neg), CEQ/CGT/CGT_UN/CLT/CLT_UN for F32/F64 with the ordered/unordered predicate mapping of isel.md 5.2 (SETO, SETUO, SETONE, SETUEQ Expand); conversions: fpext conv.r8, fpround conv.r4, sint_to_fp from I32/I64 conv.r4/conv.r8, uint_to_fp from I32 via conv.r.un (+ conv.r4 for f32; exact for 32-bit inputs), fp_to_sint/fp_to_uint conv.i4/conv.u4/conv.i/conv.u (out of range is poison), FP_TO_SINT_SAT/FP_TO_UINT_SAT Expand. uint_to_fp from I64 Custom for both f32 and f64 results: LowerUINT_TO_FP builds the sequence of decision D17 and never returns SDValue(): s = (srl x, 63); y = (or (srl x, (trunc s to i32)), (and x, s)); r = (sint_to_fp y); result = (fmul r, (sint_to_fp (add s, 1))). For x < 2^63 this is sint_to_fp x times 1; otherwise y is x/2 with the lost bit kept as a sticky bit and the multiply by 2 is exact, so the single rounding in sint_to_fp gives the correctly rounded result (compiler-rt's algorithm; its branchy form passed on every runtime, cil-runtime e05b). Do not fall back to the generic expansions: for f64 they BITCAST i64 to f64 through a stack slot (TargetLowering.cpp ~10379-10380, a frame index before M7 and a localloc frame in every function after), for f32 they build a SELECT, and conv.r.un double-rounds on .NET 8/9 and .NET Framework (cil-runtime e05). Expand: FMA, FSQRT, FSIN, FCOS, FPOW, FEXP*, FLOG*, FCEIL, FFLOOR, FTRUNC, FRINT, FNEARBYINT, FROUND, FROUNDEVEN, FMINNUM/FMAXNUM/FMINIMUM/FMAXIMUM (library calls: LowerCall diagnoses them and builds no call until M8 makes them math-library P/Invokes, D14); FABS, FCOPYSIGN and BITCAST f32<->i32 / f64<->i64 (generic expansions through a stack slot: they hit the M2 frame-index stub until M7, so M5 tests must not use them, plan 5.5); f16/bf16 are unsupported in Phase 1: their promotions call __extendhfsf2/__truncsfhf2, which LowerCall diagnoses without building a call, so the result is a diagnostic and exit code 1, never a crash.

- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/tests-ci.md section 3.4; this plan section 5.1 (method header/footer); llvm/test/tools/UpdateTestChecks/update_llc_test_checks/lit.local.cfg; llvm/test/tools/UpdateTestChecks/lit.local.cfg (the 'llc' probe) and update_llc_test_checks/nvptx-basic.test (template)
- Provides: python msil/utils/run-utc-tests.py --llc <llc.exe> <test-name>...: runs simple update_llc_test_checks .test files directly (exit 1 on any difference)

tests-ci.md 3.4 adapted to the plan 5.1 contract: ASM_FUNCTION_MSIL_RE matches a one-line '.method ... '<name>'(' header through '} // end of method '<name>''; scrub_asm_msil; get_run_handler returns the MSIL handler when the triple ends with '-msil' before the arch-prefix table; add_checks gains an optional check_label_format (default unchanged) and update_llc_test_checks.py passes MSIL_CHECK_LABEL_FORMAT ('.method {{.*}}'<name>'(') for prefixes whose RUN triple ends in -msil. msil-basic.test mirrors nvptx-basic.test: '# REQUIRES: msil-registered-target', 'cp -f %S/Inputs/msil-basic.ll %t.ll && %update_llc_test_checks %t.ll', 'diff -u %S/Inputs/msil-basic.ll.expected %t.ll'. It never runs on this Windows host: llvm/test/tools/UpdateTestChecks/lit.local.cfg sets the llc-binary feature only when a file named exactly 'llc' exists in the tools directory (it is llc.exe here), so the whole directory is UNSUPPORTED; do not change that upstream file. Instead write msil/utils/run-utc-tests.py: for each named test of llvm/test/tools/UpdateTestChecks/update_llc_test_checks it reads the two RUN lines of the 'cp -f %S/Inputs/<f> %t.ll && %update_llc_test_checks %t.ll' / 'diff -u %S/Inputs/<f>.expected %t.ll' form (anything else is an error), copies the input into a scratch directory, runs 'python llvm/utils/update_llc_test_checks.py --llc-binary <llc> --version=1 <copy>' (the arguments lit.local.cfg would add) and compares the result with the .expected file ignoring CR at end of line; it prints a unified diff and exits 1 on any difference or error. The gate runs it on msil-basic and on the upstream x86-basic as the regression check of the asm.py change. No behaviour change for other targets.

### M6. Control flow

**Goal.** Branches, loops, fused compare-and-branch, switch through the CIL switch opcode on an int32 index (D35), unreachable/trap, and branch analysis for the generic MI passes. First C programs with loops, switch and recursion run at -O2; msil-verify is clean for all of them.

**Header changes:**
- none

**Work packages**

#### M6.a Control-flow ISel and branch analysis (implement, ~900 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrControl.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrInfo.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrInfo.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md sections 2.8-2.10, 5.3, 10.7, 11.2, 11.6, 11.7; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/passes-frame.md sections 5.3-5.4; llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssemblyInstrInfo.cpp (analyzeBranch etc.); this plan decisions D34, D35
- Provides: opcodes BEQ_*, BNE_UN_*, BLT_*, BLT_UN_*, BLE_*, BLE_UN_*, BGT_*, BGT_UN_*, BGE_*, BGE_UN_* for I32/I64/F32/F64; `MSILISD::BR_TABLE`

Patterns: br -> BR; brcond on an i32 condition -> BR_IF (brtrue) / BR_UNLESS (brfalse); fused brcond(setcc) -> B{EQ,NE_UN,LT,LT_UN,LE,LE_UN,GT,GT_UN,GE,GE_UN}_{I32,I64,F32,F64} with the verified integer and FP mapping (isel.md 5.3; FP blt = OLT, blt.un = ULT, bne.un = UNE, and so on). BR_JT Custom (LowerBR_JT) -> MSILISD::BR_TABLE(index, MBBs..., default) -> BR_TABLE_I32. The index is already i32 because getJumpTableRegTy returns i32 since M2.f (decision D35): SelectionDAGBuilder range-checks the full-width value and only then truncates, so a 64-bit switch value prints as 'conv.i4' followed by 'switch'. CIL switch on a native int fails ILVerify with StackUnexpected (review experiment artifacts/review-cil/sw.il), which is why there is no BR_TABLE_I64. Never remove LLVM's range check (no WebAssemblyFixBrTableDefaults-style pass); an index outside the table is only possible when the default is unreachable, which is UB. unreachable becomes TRAP (TrapUnreachable is set); debugtrap also TRAP in Phase 1; indirectbr is handled by IndirectBrExpand (already in the pipeline). SELECT_* and emitSelect exist since M4.b; keep them and the CALL_RESULTS dispatch unchanged. MSILInstrInfo: analyzeBranch, insertBranch, removeBranch and reverseBranchCondition as WebAssembly minus the CFGStackified check, extended to the fused branches with the FP-specific inverse table of isel.md 11.7 (return true when an FP condition cannot be reversed exactly).

- FP branch inversion correctness (isel 11.7); switch semantics for negative/large indices; LLVM's range check never removed.
- No structured-CFG assumptions left from WebAssembly.

**Rebuild cost.** MSIL target TUs + relink: ~5-15 min.

### M7. Memory, static frames and fences

**Goal.** Loads and stores of every scalar width with unaligned./volatile. prefixes, the localloc static frame with FP-relative frame indices and over-alignment above 8 bytes (D13), memcpy/memset/memmove lowering, fabs/copysign and bitcasts through memory, and compiler/system fences (D36); dynamic alloca diagnosed. C programs run at -O0, so every earlier C test switches to all optimization levels.

**Depends on:** M6.

**Header changes:**
- none

**Work packages**

#### M7.a Loads, stores, memory flags, memory intrinsics and fences (implement, ~800 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrMemory.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILSetMemFlags.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILSelectionDAGInfo.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILSelectionDAGInfo.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/wasm-inventory.md section 3.6.5; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md sections 2.14-2.15, 5.5, 10.6, 11.3; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/cil-runtime.md (e04 memory, e19 memmove); llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssemblySetP2AlignOperands.cpp; llvm/lib/Target/AArch64/AArch64InstrAtomics.td:17-19 (atomic_fence patterns); llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssemblyRegStackify.cpp query() ~172-250; this plan decisions D15, D21, D36
- Provides: opcodes LDIND_I1/U1/I2/U2/I4/I/R4/R8, STIND_I1/I2/I4/I/R4/R8, CPBLK, INITBLK, MEMMOVE; memflags encoding (bits 0-2 unaligned N, bit 3 volatile); `MSILISD::CPBLK, MSILISD::INITBLK, MSILISD::MEMMOVE`; MEMORY_BARRIER (call void [mscorlib]System.Threading.Interlocked::MemoryBarrier()); atomic_fence patterns (singlethread -> generic MEMBARRIER)

Records: LDIND_* and STIND_* with a leading memflags_op immediate then the address (I64) [then the value]; no offset operand. Patterns: i32 loads (ldind.i4), sext/zext i8/i16 extloads to i32 (ldind.i1/u1/i2/u2), i64 and pointer loads ldind.i, f32/f64 ldind.r4/r8; stores stind.*, truncstores i32->i8/i16 (stind.i1/i2). i64 extloads, i64 truncstores and f64<-f32 extloads are Expand (set in M7.b's ctor; coordinate by name). MSILSetMemFlags (copy the structure of WebAssemblySetP2AlignOperands): after ISel, for every LDIND/STIND/CPBLK/INITBLK with a MachineMemOperand set the memflags immediate: 'unaligned. N' with N = largest of 1/2/4 not above the access alignment when alignment < access size, and the volatile bit when the memoperand is volatile; the InstPrinter (printMemFlagsOperand from M2.c) prints the prefixes on their own lines. MSILSelectionDAGInfo (decision D15, never return SDValue()): memcpy with a constant length <= UINT32_MAX -> MSILISD::CPBLK(dst, src, len:i32); other memcpy and every memmove -> MSILISD::MEMMOVE(src, dst, len:i64) printed as 'conv.i8', 'dup', 'call void [mscorlib]System.Buffer::MemoryCopy(void*, void*, int64, int64)' (StackPeakExtra 1); memset -> MSILISD::INITBLK(dst, val:i32, len:i32), a variable i64 length truncated with conv.i4 (documented 4 GiB limit). Atomic loads/stores stay unsupported (max atomic size 0). Fences (decision D36; clang turns 'asm volatile("" ::: "memory")' into 'fence syncscope("singlethread") seq_cst', M1.d, and ISD::ATOMIC_FENCE has no default handling: Legal without a pattern is 'Cannot select', Expand is a __sync_synchronize libcall): in MSILInstrMemory.td add 'def : Pat<(atomic_fence (timm), 0), (MEMBARRIER)>;' (the AArch64 precedent; the generic TargetOpcode::MEMBARRIER has hasSideEffects and no memoperands, so the copied RegStackify query() treats it as Write+Effects and never moves a load or store across it, and the base AsmPrinter prints it as the comment '// MEMBARRIER') and a MEMORY_BARRIER record printing 'call void [mscorlib]System.Threading.Interlocked::MemoryBarrier()' (hasSideEffects, mayLoad, mayStore) selected by 'def : Pat<(atomic_fence (timm), (timm)), (MEMORY_BARRIER)>;' for every other scope; verify the pattern order (the scope-0 pattern must win; add AddedComplexity if needed) with msil-tblgen.ps1.

DYNAMIC_STACKALLOC, STACKSAVE, STACKRESTORE and llvm.frameaddress -> DiagnosticInfoUnsupported ('dynamic alloca / VLA is not supported for MSIL yet (phase 3 shadow stack)') returning a well-formed dummy value. **Exit criteria**
- Every C test so far passes at -O0 and -O2 on .NET 8, WSL .NET 10 and .NET Framework; 04-frames and 05-memory also pass with DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0.
- localloc only ever executes with just its size on the stack (StackCheck + jitall clean); 16-byte-aligned objects are 16-aligned in small frames on every runtime.
- memmove semantics hold for overlapping ranges; unaligned/volatile prefixes printed where required; PEVerify accepts the MemoryCopy call and nothing else of its kind.
- Compiler barriers compile (no crash) and system fences call Interlocked::MemoryBarrier.
- Dynamic alloca fails with the documented diagnostic (exit code 1, no crash marker).

**Review focus** (in addition to the three standing lenses)
- Frame layout correctness (offsets, over-alignment, arguments whose address is taken).
- Memory-op typing (native int addresses, no int64), prefix encoding, cpblk/initblk size limits.
- localloc + RegStackify interaction; .locals never 'init' (passes-frame 6.6).
- Fence lowering keeps memory operations ordered through RegStackify; MEMBARRIER really is a comment-only pseudo.

**Rebuild cost.** MSIL target TUs + relink: ~5-15 min.

### M8. Globals, module initializer and P/Invoke output

**Goal.** Global variables live in one unmanaged data segment that <Module>::.cctor allocates and fills from an RVA blob, with relocations and llvm.global_ctors; code addresses globals through per-global initonly fields; undefined functions that are Phase-1 imports (puts, putchar, the C math library, msil-import-module) become per-triple P/Invokes and every other undefined function is a diagnostic (D14), so puts output works end to end (Design.md section 12's hard-coded puts, generalized to a small import table).

**Depends on:** M7.

**Header changes:**
- none

**Work packages**

#### M8.a Global addresses, function addresses, the Phase-1 import table and library-call policy (implement, ~600 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrInfo.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLoweringCall.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILUtilities.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILUtilities.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md sections 2.7, 5.7, 7, 11.2; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/asmprinter.md section 11 (per-global field form); this plan decision D14
- Provides: `MSILISD::DATA_ADDR, MSILISD::FUNC_ADDR, MSILISD::EXT_SYM`; `GLOBAL_ADDR/FUNC_ADDR patterns`; std::optional<StringRef> MSIL::getPInvokeModule(const Triple &TT, StringRef Name, const Function *F = nullptr); StringRef MSIL::getPInvokeEntry(StringRef Name, const Function *F) (MSILUtilities.h)

LowerGlobalAddress: data -> MSILISD::DATA_ADDR(TargetGlobalAddress with offset) -> GLOBAL_ADDR (offset folding allowed for data); a function used as a value -> MSILISD::FUNC_ADDR -> FUNC_ADDR (ldftn; calls through it come in M9); thread-local globals, GlobalTLSAddress and BlockAddress -> diagnostics. LowerExternalSymbol -> MSILISD::EXT_SYM. Phase-1 import table (decision D14) in MSILUtilities.cpp: MSIL::getPInvokeModule returns the library for puts and putchar (C library: linux-gnu and linux-musl "libc", windows-msvc "ucrtbase", windows-gnu "msvcrt"), for the math functions of D14 and their f-suffixed variants (math library: linux-gnu "libm.so.6" because glibc keeps libm separate and CoreCLR special-cases only "libc"; linux-musl "libc"; windows-msvc "ucrtbase"; windows-gnu "msvcrt"), and for any function with the "msil-import-module" attribute (its value; "msil-import-name" overrides the entry point through getPInvokeEntry); std::nullopt for everything else. Library-call policy in LowerCall for ExternalSymbol callees: names starting with "__" (compiler-rt and __atomic_* helpers such as __divti3, __mulsc3, __extendhfsf2) -> DiagnosticInfoUnsupported "runtime helper '<name>' is not available for MSIL yet (phase 3)"; names getPInvokeModule accepts (sqrt, floor, fmod, fmin, ...) are lowered as calls to the external symbol and become P/Invokes; any other name -> DiagnosticInfoUnsupported "library call '<name>' is not a Phase-1 import". Every diagnosed call builds no call node (M4 rule). memcpy/memset/memmove never reach here (M7).

MSILDataCollector records bytes (emitBytes, emitFill, integer values) and turns emitValueImpl expressions into absolute bytes, MSILReloc {Site, Target, Addend, Size 4|8} or MSILDiff; implement every pure virtual of MCStreamer at HEAD; errors via LLVMContext::emitError naming the global ('unsupported constant expression', 'function address + offset', 'address of a non-global'). **Exit criteria**
- puts output, a libm call and global data work end to end on .NET 8 (ucrtbase), WSL .NET 10 (libc, libm.so.6) and .NET Framework.
- RVA data is never written; '&(label)' never appears; every global access goes through its initonly field.
- Undefined functions outside the import table, external globals, TLS and other unsupported kinds fail with diagnostics (exit code 1, no crash marker).
- All emitted modules assemble and verify.

**Review focus** (in addition to the three standing lenses)
- Data capture fidelity (padding, relocations, symbol differences), layout alignment, .cctor ordering.
- P/Invoke correctness: blittable signatures, preservesig, per-triple library names, no DisableRuntimeMarshalling in Phase 1.
- Robustness of the OutStreamer swap; fallback readiness.
- Import table matches D14 exactly per triple; no undefined function silently becomes a runtime failure.

**Rebuild cost.** MSIL target TUs + relink: ~5-15 min.

### M9. Function pointers, prototype fix-ups and aggregates

**Goal.** Function pointers within the module (ldftn + managed calli), K&R and mismatched-prototype calls through AddMissingPrototypes/FixFunctionBitcasts, the 'returned' optimization, and byval/sret aggregates as clang emits them for SysV x86-64 and Win64. Calls to variadic functions stay diagnosed (phase 3).

**Depends on:** M8.

**Header changes:**
- none

**Work packages**

#### M9.a Indirect calls, calli signatures and byval arguments (implement, ~600 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILInstrCall.td`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLoweringCall.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelDAGToDAG.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILMCInstLower.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILMCInstLower.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MCTargetDesc/MSILInstPrinter.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MCTargetDesc/MSILInstPrinter.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/isel.md sections 2.12, 8.2; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/asmprinter.md section 6.4; llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssemblyISelLowering.cpp (byval in LowerCall), WebAssemblyMCInstLower.cpp:274-301
- Consumes: MSILAsmPrinter::internSignature (M2.d); MSILMemberRefExpr::createSig (M2.c)

Indirect callees (anything but GlobalAddress/ExternalSymbol) -> CALL_INDIRECT with the callee as the last register operand (calli order) and calling convention Managed; MCInstLower builds the MSIL::Signature from the MI (defs -> results, explicit register uses minus the trailing callee -> params, toValType), interns it via Printer.internSignature and emits MSILMemberRefExpr::createSig; the InstPrinter prints 'calli <ret>(<params>)'. byval arguments: copy into a new stack object with an always-inline memcpy as WebAssembly's LowerCall does (uses the M7 frame); sret stays a plain pointer argument; inalloca/preallocated -> diagnostic.

#### M9.b IR fix-up passes (copied) (implement, ~500 lines copied)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILAddMissingPrototypes.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILFixFunctionBitcasts.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILOptimizeReturned.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssembly{AddMissingPrototypes,FixFunctionBitcasts,OptimizeReturned}.cpp; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/asmprinter.md section 7.4; this plan decision D18, D27

Copy the three WebAssembly passes (D30 header line, no new-PM class). AddMissingPrototypes acts on the "no-prototype" attribute that clang sets for MSIL triples (M1.d). FixFunctionBitcasts creates wrappers for calls whose call-site type differs from the callee's type, including K&R variadic-typed calls to defined non-variadic functions; REMOVE WebAssembly's main renaming (__original_main and the argc/argv wrapper), because '<msil>Main' calls main with its own signature (D27). OptimizeReturned mechanical. LowerCall's mismatched-signature check (M4) stays as a backstop.

- Owned files: `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/call-indirect.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/ldftn-calli.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/fnptr-table.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/function-bitcasts.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/add-prototypes.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/returned.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/byval.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/sret.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/struct-args-win64.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/struct-args-sysv.ll`, `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/varargs-call-error.ll`

Status.md: what Phase 1 supports and what it does not (varargs, TLS, dynamic alloca, long double = double, Darwin/i686, object files, BCL intrinsics, the codegen switches for newer .NET APIs of Design.md 7.1), the verification policy, known runtime differences (.NET 8 vs 10 vs Framework), and a 'Proposed Design.md updates' section (Design.md itself is user-owned and must not be edited by agents) that records at least: the section 12 command 'dotnet prog.dll' needs prog.runtimeconfig.json (or 'dotnet exec --runtimeconfig'), which the user or the build system writes, never the compiler (Design.md 8; tests-ci E2: rc 131 without it); the verification criterion is D21, not the literal ILVerify sentence; the Phase-1 import table of D14 instead of P/Invoking every undefined function; __ELF__ on Linux MSIL triples (section 10 decision 9); localloc alignment (D13); and the roughly 1.5 MB main-thread stack of .NET versus native as a known difference for deep recursion.

```text
12. pwsh -NoProfile -Command ". D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/build/msil-env.ps1; python D:/llvm-msil/msil/utils/update-expected.py --clang D:/llvm-msil/build/bin/clang.exe --check D:/llvm-msil/msil/test/M1"

```

**Exit criteria**
- At least 25 programs (11-programs plus the M9 struct and function-pointer tests) pass at -O0 and -O2 with the native oracle required.
- Legs green: .NET 8 (tiered and TieredCompilation=0), .NET 10, .NET Framework 4.8 (Windows), WSL .NET 10 with x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil (tiered and TieredCompilation=0), Linux ilasm inside WSL, modern Windows ilasm, ildasm round trip.
- msil-verify (ILVerify allow-list + PEVerify), jitall and MSILStackCheck report no stack-shape errors.
- The local gate runs the same msil/utils/ci scripts as msil-ci.yml; enabling the workflow remains the user's decision.
- Documentation committed, including the 'Proposed Design.md updates' list.

**Review focus** (in addition to the three standing lenses)
- Programs are UB-free and meaningful (native -O0/-O2 agree); coverage maps to every Design.md 12 example.
- Verification policy is enforced, not advisory; allow-list unchanged or justified.
- Docs match behaviour; Design.md untouched (proposals only).

**Rebuild cost.** MSIL target TUs + relink if fixes are needed: ~5-15 min; the full lit legs take a few minutes.

### M11. Upstream-merge follow-ups: crash and pipeline fixes, upstream-hook coverage, more gate legs

**Goal.** Close the ten items that the upstream merge of 2026-10-19 deferred (section 12 row 'Deferred after the upstream merge'; the numbers (1)-(10) below are that row's). Late function splitting no longer crashes the MSIL AsmPrinter (3); `llc -stop-after=msil-isel` and `-stop-before=msil-argument-move` print MIR that passes the machine verifier and reads back (4); LowerInvoke runs once and UnreachableBlockElim no longer runs a second time after CodeGenPrepare (5). Independent tests pin the aarch64 aggregate signatures that upstream de7794fcf781 changed (1), the MC assembly parser's IsMSIL hook (6) and `-mllvm` options through clang (10). A curated 'upstream-hooks' check runs the upstream regression tests of every upstream file the fork changes, proves that its list of hooked files is complete, and compiles the two hooked files that this build never compiles in a private build tree on C: (6, 7). actions/upload-artifact is pinned as upstream pins it, and a checker keeps every action pin in step after later merges (2). run-utc-tests.py (8) and the -O1/-O3/-Os/-Oz execution levels (9) become regular gate and CI legs. Documentation follows. No IL changes for any input that compiled before. The user decided on 2026-10-20 to do this before Phase 2 planning (section 12, row 'M11 added').

**Depends on:** M10 and the upstream merge 2ea3fa74b232 (section 12, 2026-10-19). Before the pre-spawn checks the orchestrator copies the recon evidence of 2026-10-20 to `llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/` (section 12, row 'M11 added'); every Reads entry below that names `llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/` points there.

**Work packages**

#### M11.a Function splitting off, verifier-clean instruction selection, one invoke lowering (implement, ~120 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILTargetMachine.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelDAGToDAG.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILArgumentMove.cpp`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILUtilities.h`, `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILUtilities.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/split.md sections 0-7 and 10; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/split-files/item3.diff; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/split-files/tools/ (relink.ps1, mkrsp.py); llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/stop-after.md sections 1-9 and 12; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/stop-after-files/ (prototype.diff, compile.ps1, link.ps1); llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/eh-passes.md sections 1-7 and 10; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/eh-passes-files/tools/ (build.ps1, ehcount.py, corpus.py, ildiff.py); llvm/lib/CodeGen/TargetPassConfig.cpp (constructor ~440-475, addPassesToHandleExceptions ~767-811, addMachinePasses ~1105-1160); llvm/lib/CodeGen/BasicBlockSections.cpp (~470-530, ~578-581); llvm/lib/CodeGen/CodeGenTargetMachineImpl.cpp (~240-250); llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssemblyTargetMachine.cpp (its addPassesToHandleExceptions override); llvm/lib/Target/WebAssembly/WebAssemblyArgumentMove.cpp; this plan decisions D8, D23, D30, D33 and sections 5.3, 5.4
- Provides: `bool MSIL::moveArgumentsToTop(MachineFunction &MF)` (MSILUtilities.h: moves every ARGUMENT_<RC> of the entry block above its first other instruction, keeping the relative order of both groups; true if an instruction moved); `void MSILPassConfig::addPassesToHandleExceptions() override` (adds no pass); the MSILPassConfig constructor forces `TM.Options.FunctionSplitting = FunctionSplittingMode::None`

Three independent fixes; the recon reports hold the reproductions, the root causes with file:line references, the rejected alternatives and verified prototypes. (1) Item 3, function splitting. TargetPassConfig's constructor applies llc's and `-mllvm`'s `-function-splitting=` to `TM.Options` after the TargetMachine exists (TargetPassConfig.cpp ~472-473), and cc1 `-fsplit-machine-functions` sets the mode before (clang BackendUtil.cpp ~432-433). With `All`, addMachinePasses adds BasicBlockSections with SplitWithPGO, which gives a profiled function (every function under `-mfs-split-ehcode`) section type Preset; the AsmPrinter then switches to the nullptr section that MSILTargetObjectFile inherits, and MCStreamer asserts 'Cannot switch to a null section!'. Give the MSILPassConfig constructor a body that sets `TM.Options.FunctionSplitting = FunctionSplittingMode::None;` with the comment of split.md section 7 (CIL methods have no sections, so no function is ever split; dropped silently like the basic block sections in the MSILTargetMachine constructor (D8), but here, because the base constructor has just applied the command-line mode and addMachinePasses reads it when it builds the pipeline). A reset in the MSILTargetMachine constructor alone leaves llc and `-mllvm` crashing (verified); do not add one there. No header change (FunctionSplittingMode is in llvm/Target/TargetOptions.h, already included) and no clang change: the driver already rejects `-fsplit-machine-functions`, `-fbasic-block-sections=all|list=`, `-fbasic-block-address-map` and `-fpartition-static-data-sections` on every MSIL triple, because their object format is not ELF (`-fbasic-block-sections=labels`, a deprecated alias, passes the driver as `-fbasic-block-address-map`, which MSILPrepareIR already ignores with a warning). Do not add section hooks to MSILTargetObjectFile or an `isFunctionSafeToSplit` override (split.md section 6, options D and E: BasicBlockSections would still run after RegStackify, ExplicitLocals and RegNumbering). (2) Item 4, stop points. Upstream 663669080864 makes llc run the machine verifier 'At end of pipeline' whenever it stops before code emission, and the MIR parser verifies on read. Every MSIL instruction carries `implicit-def dead $arguments`, ARGUMENT_<RC> reads `implicit $arguments`, and the ScheduleDAG scheduler can put an ARGUMENT after another instruction, which the verifier reports as 'Using an undefined physical register'. Make the output of instruction selection clean (stop-after.md option A, section 9; the recon's inline prototype is stop-after-files/prototype.diff): move the static `argumentMove` of MSILArgumentMove.cpp into MSILUtilities as `MSIL::moveArgumentsToTop` (declared next to `getCopyOpcodeForRegClass`, with a `class MachineFunction;` forward declaration if the header lacks one; use `llvm::make_early_inc_range` for the second loop); in `MSILDAGToDAGISel::runOnMachineFunction` keep the `MF.setUseDebugInstrRef(false)` call, call `SelectionDAGISel::runOnMachineFunction(MF)`, then `MSIL::moveArgumentsToTop(MF)`, and return the base's result, with a comment naming the scheduler, the end-of-pipeline verifier (663669080864) and the MIR parser's verify-on-read, and include "MSILUtilities.h"; `MSILArgumentMoveLegacy::runOnMachineFunction` keeps its LLVM_DEBUG banner and returns `MSIL::moveArgumentsToTop(MF)`, and the file comment says that instruction selection already moves the ARGUMENTs and that the pass stays in the pipeline (plan 5.3 and pipeline.ll unchanged) for MIR input such as reg-argument.mir. The DBG_VALUEs that SelectionDAGISel puts after each ARGUMENT stay where they are, so they follow the moved ARGUMENTs (M11.b tests a debug-info function). Do not change the .td operand lists (plan 5.4 keeps `implicit-def dead $arguments`) or MSILRegisterInfo (ARGUMENTS stays unreserved), and do not use FailsVerification or `-disable-mir-output-verify` (stop-after.md section 7, options B-F). (3) Item 5, invoke lowering. MSILPassConfig::addIRPasses lowers invokes early (the WebAssembly no-EH shape copied in M2), and TargetPassConfig::addPassesToHandleExceptions adds LowerInvoke and UnreachableBlockElim again after CodeGenPrepare for ExceptionHandling::None; upstream fa24f6dba7cd made that hook virtual. Declare `void addPassesToHandleExceptions() override;` after `void addIRPasses() override;` in class MSILPassConfig and define it after MSILPassConfig::addIRPasses with no addPass call, the comment of eh-passes.md section 7 (the exception model is always None, D8; addIRPasses has already lowered every invoke into a call and removed the landing pads that became unreachable, before the target and generic IR passes; TargetPassConfig would add LowerInvoke and UnreachableBlockElim a second time after CodeGenPrepare) and its assert that `TM->getMCAsmInfo().getExceptionHandlingType()` is `ExceptionHandling::None` (add `#include "llvm/MC/MCAsmInfo.h"`). Keep the early LowerInvoke and UnreachableBlockElim in addIRPasses (WebAssembly's shape after fa24f6dba7cd; deleting them instead, option B, would let invokes and dead landing pads reach IndirectBrExpand, LSR and CodeGenPrepare) and extend their comment to say that addPassesToHandleExceptions adds nothing. Checks: msil-syntax.ps1 on the four changed .cpp files (MSILTargetMachine.cpp, MSILISelDAGToDAG.cpp, MSILArgumentMove.cpp, MSILUtilities.cpp) and on MSILUtilities.h; git-clang-format on the changed lines. The WP cannot build the shared tree, but it may verify with a private llc and clang as the recon did, never writing D:\llvm-msil\build: compile the four changed TUs into scratch with their compile_commands.json commands (output paths redirected, as stop-after-files/compile.ps1 does for one TU), then let split-files/tools/mkrsp.py build the llc and clang link lines with those objects ahead of the build tree's libraries and link with lld-link. split-files/tools/relink.ps1 compiles only MSILTargetMachine.cpp with hard-coded flags, so generalize it to the four TUs first. Then run the reproductions of split.md section 2, stop-after.md section 2 (with stop-after-files/run/dbg.c) and eh-passes.md section 2. The recon measured byte-identical IL on its whole corpus for all three fixes; any IL difference is a bug. llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/pipeline.ll, which pins the old double lowering, belongs to M11.b and fails until both WPs are in.

If one exposes a compiler bug, report it with a reproducer: the fix goes through a fix-loop ownership grant (section 1.7a). (1) Item 1, aarch64 aggregates. Upstream de7794fcf781 passes a non-HFA aggregate argument of fewer than 8 bytes as `iN` of its exact size (i8 ... i56, formerly i64) on all four aarch64 MSIL triples, so 1-4-byte aggregates are now `int32` IL parameters and 5-7-byte ones stay `native int`; results did not change (legs.md item 1 has the full table). `clang/test/CodeGen/MSIL/aarch64-aggregate-abi.c` (new, `// REQUIRES: msil-registered-target`; prototype legs-proto/aarch64-aggregate-abi.c): the header comment says why the test exists; IR RUN lines `%clang_cc1 -triple <t> -emit-llvm -o - %s | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=IR,IR-LNX` for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil and aarch64-unknown-linux-musl-msil and `IR,IR-WIN` for aarch64-pc-windows-msvc-msil and aarch64-w64-windows-gnu-msil; IL RUN lines `%clang_cc1 -triple <t> -S -O2 -o %t.<x>.il %s` and `FileCheck %s --check-prefix=IL --implicit-check-not=int64 --input-file=%t.<x>.il` for all four triples, plus -O0 for the gnu and msvc triples; `%if ilasm %{ %ilasm-verify -arm64 -output=... %}` on the gnu -O2 and msvc -O0 outputs. One function per shape (structs of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16 and 24 bytes, int+float, char+float, the HFAs float2, float3, double4, double1 and float[3], a pointer pair), each with an `IR-LABEL: define {{.*}}i24 @f3(i24 %x.coerce)`-style line (HFA rows: alignstack(8) on Linux only) and an exact `IL: {{^}}.method public static int32 'f3'(int32) cil managed{{$}}` line; call sites through noinline callees that store to a volatile global (`g3(struct S3)`, `g5(struct S5)`, `call_small`: `IR: call void @g3(i24`, `IL: call void 'g3'(int32)`, `IL: call void 'g5'(native int)`), because a `return x` callee is deleted at -O2; leave the vector_size HVAs out. `llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/struct-args-aapcs64.ll` (new, the AAPCS64 twin of struct-args-sysv.ll and struct-args-win64.ll): the IR that clang -O2 emits for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil (generate it, then remove the datalayout and the triple), with callees taking and returning i8, i16, i24, i32, i40, i48, i56, i64, `[2 x i64]`, `[2 x ptr]`, `[2 x float] alignstack(8)`, `[4 x double] alignstack(8)`, HFA struct results and an indirect `sret` case, and callers that build each coerced value from memory; RUN lines for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil and aarch64-pc-windows-msvc-msil at -O0 and -O2 with `-asm-verbose=false -verify-machineinstrs`, a shared `SIG:` prefix for every method header, CHECK lines for the call-site packing (`ldind.u2`, `ldind.u1`, `ldc.i4.s 16`, `shl`, `or`, then `call void 'g3'(int32)`), `--implicit-check-not=int64`, and `%if ilasm %{ ... %ilasm-verify -arm64 ... %}`. Execution stays x86_64-only (D6). (2) Item 6, `clang/test/CodeGen/MSIL/cc1as-unsupported.s` (new; text hooks-artifacts/cc1as-unsupported.s, spec hooks.md section 3): `# REQUIRES: msil-registered-target`; `not %clang -cc1as -triple <t> -filetype asm|null %s ... 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --implicit-check-not="PLEASE submit" --implicit-check-not="Stack dump"` for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil (`-filetype asm -o -`) and aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil and aarch64-w64-windows-gnu-msil (`-filetype null`), `# CHECK: error in backend: assembly parsing is not supported for MSIL`, a native control `%if x86-registered-target %{ %clang -cc1as -triple x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -filetype null %s %}`, body `nop`; never `-filetype obj` (an upstream-generic assertion for targets without an MCAsmBackend). Without the hook the assembly parser dereferences a null platform parser. (3) Item 10, `clang/test/CodeGen/MSIL/mllvm.c` (new, `// REQUIRES: msil-registered-target`; prototype legs-proto/mllvm.c, spec legs.md item 10): `-mllvm -msil-assembly-name=foo` gives `.assembly 'foo'` (default `.assembly 'mllvm'`) through `%clang_cc1 -triple x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil`, `%clang --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil` and `%clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil`, and the last of two occurrences wins; `-###` shows `"-cc1" {{.*}}"-triple" "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc{{[0-9.]*}}-msil"` and then `"-mllvm" "-msil-assembly-name=foo"`; `not %clang_cc1 ... -mllvm -msil-no-such-option` reports 'Unknown command line argument'; global pass-manager options (`-print-after=msil-reg-stackify`, `-debug-pass=Structure` listing CodeGen Prepare, MSIL Instruction Selection, MSIL Register Stackify and MSIL Assembly Printer in order); per-context CodeGen options (`-print-after-isel` with `ARGUMENT_I32`, `-disable-cgp` through the driver with no 'CodeGen Prepare', `-verify-machineinstrs` with 'Verify generated machine code' after 'MSIL Register Stackify'); and a per-context IR-library option (`-O1` with and without `-mllvm -instcombine-code-sinking=0` on `void g(int c, int a, int b) { int d = a / b; if (c) use(d); }` with `use` defined through a volatile store: brfalse before div by default, div before brfalse with the option). Do not use `-stop-after` (item 4) or `-stackmap-version` (MSIL emits no stack maps), and do not count LowerInvoke (item 5 belongs to M11.b). Gate step 13 fails if one of the four files is missing; M11.d's manifest also names cc1as-unsupported.s as the fork test of llvm/lib/MC/MCParser/AsmParser.cpp.

#### M11.d Upstream-hooks check, hooks compile coverage, action pins, gate and CI wiring (infra, ~900 lines)

Items 2, 6 (compile coverage) and 7, and the wiring of the new checks into the gate script and CI. Spawned after M11.e hands over, so its run-m1-gate.ps1 check sees the final leg scripts. (1) The manifest `msil/utils/upstream-hooks.txt`, from the draft hooks-artifacts/upstream-hooks.txt (format in its header): one `hook <path>` block for each of the 36 upstream files the fork changes (hooks.md section 1.1), each with at least one of `lit <path-or-glob>`, `gtest <exe> [<filter>]`, `compile`, `utc <test>...` (documentation only: M11.e's utc leg runs them) or `none <reason>`, plus `fork <test>` lines naming the fork tests that pin the MSIL side (for llvm/lib/MC/MCParser/AsmParser.cpp: clang/test/CodeGen/MSIL/cc1as-unsupported.s, which M11.c writes); top-level `fork-only <path>` lines for fork files in upstream directories (.github/workflows/msil-ci.yml, clang/lib/Basic/Targets/MSIL.h, llvm/include/llvm/MC/MCSectionMSIL.h, clang/test/Driver/msil-toolchain.c, clang/test/Preprocessor/init-msil.c and the three msil-basic files of update_llc_test_checks), `switch-default <path>` (llvm/lib/MC/MCAsmBackend.cpp, llvm/lib/ExecutionEngine/JITLink/JITLink.cpp), `switch-other <path> <reason>` (llvm/lib/MC/StringTableBuilder.cpp: its `case XCOFF:` belongs to StringTableBuilder::Kind, not to an object-format enum), `allow <test> <reason>` (empty at introduction; only a per-file environment failure whose reason names the missing tool, never a directory, a glob or a real mismatch) and `min-pass 280`. The lit lines expand to 301 inputs: the 298 of hooks-artifacts/curated-paths.txt (the draft manifest lacks `lit clang/test/Frontend/embed-bitcode.ll`; add it to the llvm/lib/Bitcode/Writer/BitcodeWriter.cpp block), clang/test/Driver/cl-options.c and clang/test/Driver/clang_f_opts.c under clang/lib/Driver/ToolChains/Clang.cpp (the only upstream tests of its /GS and -fms-volatile hunks; they need llvm-profdata, which M11 adds to the build targets), and clang/test/Driver/spirv-openmp-toolchain.c under clang/lib/Driver/ToolChain.cpp (the curated list never reaches getLinkerWrapper, the one hunk there that changes control flow for native triples; this test builds a clang-linker-wrapper job, has no REQUIRES line and passed here in 2 s during planning). `--list-lit` must print exactly those 301 paths. Leave out the other 10 tests of hooks.md section 2.1 that need tools this build lacks (llvm-lto2, llvm-readobj, llvm-nm, llvm-objdump, llvm-mc, llvm-dwarfdump, llvm-objcopy) and the slow fsanitize.c, init.c and predefined-arch-macros.c (cheaper siblings cover their hooks). The manifest header documents the format, the base resolution of (2) and that the lit leg passes the list through a response file. (2) `msil/utils/ci/check-upstream-hooks.py` (Python standard library, from the prototype check_manifest.py). `--check`: the base is, in this order, `$env:MSIL_UPSTREAM_BASE`; `MERGE_HEAD` when `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` succeeds (an upstream merge in progress, which the merge workflow gates before it commits; the diff against MERGE_HEAD is then exactly the fork's footprint on the new upstream); else the second parent of `git log --first-parent --merges -1 --grep='^\[MSIL\] Merge upstream llvm-project main at ' --format=%P HEAD`. It prints the base it chose and why; finding none (for example in a shallow clone) is an error that names the reason. The changed paths are `git diff --name-only <base>` (against the working tree) plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, so a milestone's uncommitted work counts; every changed path outside the fork-only prefixes (llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/, llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL/, llvm/docs/MSIL/, llvm/unittests/Target/MSIL/, clang/test/CodeGen/MSIL/, msil/, .github/msil/) and not marked fork-only needs a block; a block or fork-only line for an unchanged path is stale; every lit glob must match and every fork test must exist; an `allow` line is rejected when its test contains '*' or '?', names a directory or a path that is not one of the lit inputs, or has an empty reason; and every file that `git grep -l -E` finds in the whole monorepo (the exhaustive object-format switches, also in unbuilt projects such as lld or bolt) for `case (llvm::)?Triple::XCOFF *:`, `case (llvm::)?MCContext::IsXCOFF *:` or the unqualified `case +(XCOFF|IsXCOFF) *:([^:]|$)` (class scope or `using enum`, as llvm/lib/TargetParser/Triple.cpp:434 is written) must name MSIL or be switch-default or switch-other. `--list-lit` prints the expanded lit inputs, one per line. `--lit-verdict <file>` reads lit's JSON report (`-o`; one `code` per executed test, test names such as 'Clang :: Driver/cl-options.c', which it maps to repository paths such as clang/test/Driver/cl-options.c) and passes when every FAIL is allow-listed, no allow-listed test PASSes (a stale entry), no test is UNRESOLVED, TIMEOUT or XPASS, and the number of PASS results (XFAIL does not count) is at least the manifest's min-pass or `--min-pass`; it prints one line per problem and the counts. `--self-test` uses a temporary directory outside the repository (removed afterwards) and must report: a planted unlisted hook, a stale block, a missing fork test, a lit glob without a match, a qualified and an unqualified switch file without an MSIL case, allow lines with a glob, a directory and an empty reason, the MERGE_HEAD base during a merge in progress (a temporary git repository, or an injectable git runner), and the lit verdicts of synthetic JSON reports (FAIL for an unlisted failure, a stale allow entry, an UNRESOLVED result, an XPASS result and a PASS count below min-pass; PASS for an allow-listed failure). Exit codes as plan-check.py (0, 1, 2). (3) `msil/utils/ci/check-action-pins.py` (item 2; Python standard library, from legs-proto/check-action-pins.py): for every `uses: <owner>/<repo>[/<path>]@<ref> # <version>` line of `.github/**/msil-*.y*ml` it compares ref and version with what the other .github YAML files use for the same action, prints `<file>:<line>: ...; upstream: <ref> # <ver> (<n> uses)` per mismatch and exits 1 on any; actions that upstream never uses (actions/setup-dotnet) are reported without failing. (4) `msil/utils/ci/upstream-hooks.ps1`, rows through ci-common.ps1 (step 'upstream-hooks'), legs in this order: `manifest` (check-upstream-hooks.py --check); `pins` (check-action-pins.py on the repository); `lit` (one msil-lit.ps1 call, as lit-legs.ps1 makes it: the first path of --list-lit is the mandatory path argument and the others go to `<build>/lit-results/upstream-hooks.rsp`, one per line, passed as `@<that file>` inside the -LitArgs value, so the list never meets the 32,767-character Windows command-line limit (about 19,300 characters as absolute paths today, and the list grows with every merge); the value is written `-LitArgs:-sv @<rsp> -o <build>/lit-results/upstream-hooks.json --xunit-xml-output=<build>/lit-results/upstream-hooks.xml` because it starts with '-' and contains a drive path, and the leg fails with a clear message if the build path contains a blank, which msil-lit.ps1 would split; log next to them; the verdict is `check-upstream-hooks.py --lit-verdict` on the JSON file, with `-MinPass` passed on as `--min-pass`); `gtest` (msil-gtest.ps1 -NoSkip on unittests/TargetParser/TargetParserTests.exe with `-Filter '*-HostTest.getMacOSHostVersion:HostTest.AIXHostVersionDetect:HostTest.AIXTargetVersionDetect:HostTest.AIXHostCPUDetect' -MinTests 700` and on unittests/MC/MCTests.exe with `-Filter '*-TargetRegistry.MSILLookupWithoutTarget<more>' -MinTests 40`, where `<more>` comes from `<build>/bin/llvm-config --targets-built`: `:Disassembler.WebAssemblyTest` when WebAssembly is not built (the CI build, msil/cmake/caches/MSIL.cmake, has X86 only) and `:Disassembler.X86Test` when X86 is not, because those tests call GTEST_SKIP without their target and -NoSkip fails a skip; the leading '*' keeps 'pwsh -File' from reading a value that starts with '-' and contains ':' as a parameter name); `compile` (item 6: in the private tree `-HooksBuildDir`, default `$env:MSIL_HOOKS_BUILD_DIR`, else `C:\llvm-msil-hooks-build`. The leg takes that tree's exclusive lock itself (`Enter-MsilBuildLock -BuildDir <tree>`) and, while it holds it, runs cmake and ninja directly; it never calls msil-configure.ps1 or msil-build.ps1, which take the same lock themselves and would wait for their own parent for up to 240 minutes. When the tree has no build.ninja, it configures it with the cmake options of hooks.md section 4.1 (projects clang;lldb, LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD=ARM, no experimental targets or external projects, tests, docs, benchmarks and examples off, every optional LLDB dependency off, and the compilers, Python and job limits of msil-configure.ps1); then `ninja -C <tree> lib\Target\ARM\AsmParser\CMakeFiles\LLVMARMAsmParser.dir\ARMAsmParser.cpp.obj`, which also generates the ARM .inc files; then on every run `msil-syntax.ps1 -BuildDir <tree> -ExtraFlags /clang:-Werror=switch` (no lock of its own) on llvm/lib/Target/ARM/AsmParser/ARMAsmParser.cpp and lldb/source/Plugins/Process/gdb-remote/GDBRemoteCommunicationClient.cpp. Never build the lldb object with ninja (its order-only edges pull in about 1,000 unrelated TUs, 19 min), never delete or clean the tree (a broken cache takes `cmake --fresh` or a new `-HooksBuildDir`), never touch D:\llvm-msil\build). Switches: `-Leg`; `-NoManifest` and `-NoCompile` print a SKIP line for their leg and write no row; `-MinPass` overrides the manifest's min-pass; `-SelfTest` runs check-upstream-hooks.py --self-test, the MCTests filter derivation for the target lists 'X86' (excludes Disassembler.WebAssemblyTest) and 'X86 WebAssembly' (excludes neither), and a mutation check of the compile leg: copies of both TUs with their MSIL case line removed, under `[IO.Path]::GetTempPath()` and removed afterwards, must fail `msil-syntax.ps1 -BuildDir <hooks tree> -FlagsFrom <the original TU> -ExtraInclude <its source directory> -ExtraFlags /clang:-Werror=switch <copy>` with 'not handled in switch', and the originals must pass (the hooks tree must exist: without build.ninja the self-test fails and says to run the compile leg first); no self-test file is ever written inside the repository. Exit 1 if any row failed. The header documents the legs, that the script is Windows-only, and the costs: manifest ~11 s, pins ~1 s, lit ~1 min, gtest 10-25 s, compile ~47 s in steady state, ~13 min for a new tree and 5-13 min after an upstream merge; the existing tree is about 460 MB (the recon also built the lldb object there), about 140 MB when recreated by the script. (5) `msil/utils/run-m1-gate.ps1`: a new step 5 'upstream-hooks' after lit-legs (ci-sh becomes step 6) that runs upstream-hooks.ps1 with every leg when configure and build passed (a failed configure or build skips it, as it skips the unit tests and the lit legs), then checks the rows manifest, pins, lit, gtest and compile with Test-ChildRows; a `-SkipUpstreamHooks` switch like `-SkipUnitTests`; the header names the new lit legs utc and more-levels (M11.e) and says that the format and scope checks are M11 gate steps 25 and 26. (6) `.github/workflows/msil-ci.yml`: lines 179 and 289 pin `actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2` (upstream's pin since d770860630c7); the Windows job's Build step gets `id: build`, and a new step 'Upstream hook tests (msil/utils/ci/upstream-hooks.ps1)' after the test legs runs `pwsh -NoProfile -File msil/utils/ci/upstream-hooks.ps1 -NoCompile -NoManifest -MinPass 250` with `if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.build.outcome == 'success' }}`, so it runs after failed unit tests or test legs, as run-m1-gate.ps1 does, and is skipped only when the build failed. Its comment says why: the checkout is shallow (no merge commit for the manifest leg), the hooks tree is a development-host cost, and the CI build has no WebAssembly target, so the list's WebAssembly tests are UNSUPPORTED (hence the lower -MinPass; the development host's gate enforces the manifest's min-pass) and Disassembler.WebAssemblyTest is filtered out. The existing upload step already keeps build/lit-results/ (upstream-hooks.json, .xml, .log). The header comment names the new legs and this step; triggers, guards and the other pins stay as they are. (7) `msil/utils/ci/build.ps1` and `msil/utils/ci/build.sh`: `llvm-profdata` joins the ninja targets (the two scripts keep the same list), and their comments name the M11 build targets. Exception to plan section 1.3 for this WP only: it may run cmake and ninja in the private hooks tree on C: (the recon left it configured, with the ARM object built), never in D:\llvm-msil\build. Checks: check-upstream-hooks.py --self-test and --check (until M11.c hands over, the only expected problem is the missing cc1as-unsupported.s), and `--list-lit` against curated-paths.txt plus the three added tests (301 lines); `upstream-hooks.ps1 -Leg manifest,pins,gtest,compile` and `-SelfTest`, with `git status --short` unchanged afterwards; `<build>/bin/llvm-config --targets-built` and the MCTests filter the script derives from it; the lit leg through msil-lit.ps1 exactly as the gate runs it (no recon helper): against the shared build everything passes except cl-options.c and clang_f_opts.c, which fail with exit status 127 until the gate builds llvm-profdata; validate those two before hand-over in a private lit root (hooks-artifacts/gen_litroot.py) whose llvm_tools_dir and clang_tools_dir point to a scratch directory holding hard links to D:\llvm-msil\build\bin plus 'C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Professional/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin/llvm-profdata.exe' (both passed that way in about 17 s during planning), and record the result; the exact CI command `upstream-hooks.ps1 -NoCompile -NoManifest -MinPass 250` (exit 0, SKIP lines for manifest and compile, rows only for pins, lit and gtest); check-action-pins.py on the repository (0 mismatches after the bump) and on a scratch copy with one pin changed back (exit 1); `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` on msil-ci.yml; `run-m1-gate.ps1 -SkipConfigure -SkipBuild -SkipUnitTests -NoWsl -Leg expected` (shows the upstream-hooks rows).

**Exit criteria**
- Item 3: on both x86_64 MSIL triples, `llc -function-splitting=all` (also with -O0, `-mfs-split-ehcode`, `--basic-block-sections=all` or a profile, and `--basic-block-address-map`) and clang cc1 `-fsplit-machine-functions`, `-Xclang -fsplit-machine-functions` and `-mllvm -function-splitting=all` exit 0 with IL identical to the run without the option (only the existing address-map warning); `-debug-pass=Structure` shows no basic-block-sections pass; the driver still rejects the ELF-only section options on every MSIL triple and passes `-fbasic-block-sections=labels` on as the address map (function-splitting.ll, split-machine-functions.c, msil-toolchain.c).
- Item 4: `llc -stop-after=msil-isel` and `-stop-before=msil-argument-move` exit 0 on both triples at -O0 and -O2, the MIR reads back with `-run-pass=none`, and `-start-after=msil-isel` gives the full pipeline's IL, also for a function with debug info whose argument DBG_VALUEs follow the moved ARGUMENTs (stop-after-isel.ll); no MSIL test passes `-disable-mir-output-verify`; reg-argument.mir passes unchanged.
- Item 5: LowerInvoke runs once and UnreachableBlockElim twice in every MSIL pipeline, at the positions pipeline.ll pins; every existing invoke test (function-bitcasts.ll, call-errors.ll, frame-escape-errors.ll) passes unchanged.
- Items 1, 6 and 10: aarch64-aggregate-abi.c and struct-args-aapcs64.ll pin the aarch64 aggregate shapes in IR and IL on all four aarch64 MSIL triples and assemble with `-arm64`; cc1as-unsupported.s pins the IsMSIL assembly-parser hook (clean error, no crash); mllvm.c pins global and per-context `-mllvm` options through cc1 and the driver. Gate step 13 proves that every new test file exists.
- Items 6 and 7: upstream-hooks.ps1 passes with every leg: the manifest covers every upstream file the fork changes (36 hook blocks at introduction) and every exhaustive object-format switch, qualified or not, against the right base (MERGE_HEAD during a merge); the 301 curated upstream lit inputs give at least min-pass PASS results with an empty allow-list; the full TargetParserTests and MCTests pass (host-gated tests, and tests of targets the build lacks, excluded by name); ARMAsmParser.cpp and GDBRemoteCommunicationClient.cpp compile with `-Werror=switch` in the private tree; `-SelfTest` proves that each check, the allow-list rules and the lit verdict fail on a planted defect, and leaves the working tree unchanged. The residual gap is recorded (the lldb TU is syntax-checked only; no ARM or lldb test runs).
- Item 2: msil-ci.yml pins actions/upload-artifact at upstream's v7.0.2 SHA, check-action-pins.py reports 0 mismatches, and msil-ci.yml parses.
- Items 8 and 9: lit-legs.ps1 and lit-legs.sh have the default legs utc and more-levels (gate steps 20, 21 and 23); run-utc-tests.py passes its six tests; msil/test/M1 passes at O1, O3, Os and Oz on the Windows triple and, under WSL, on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil (gate step 22); run-m1-gate.ps1 and both CI jobs run the legs, and the Windows CI job also runs the upstream-hooks pins, lit and gtest legs whenever its build passed (step 17 runs that exact command).
- run-m1-gate.ps1 prints every row PASS, including the new rows; every M10 leg stays green; no IL changes for any input that compiled before M11.
- GettingStarted.md, Status.md (counts included), msil/README.md, msil/test/README.md and msil/utils/build/README.md describe the fixes, the new legs, the build targets and the upstream-hooks check.

**Review focus** (in addition to the three standing lenses)
- Items 3-5 change no IL: the function-splitting reset sits where llc, `-mllvm` and cc1 all reach it; the ARGUMENT move keeps DBG_VALUE placement and relative order; the early invoke lowering stays and nothing EH-related runs after CodeGenPrepare.
- Upstream idioms and minimal diffs: WebAssembly's post-fa24f6dba7cd shape for item 5, MSILArgumentMove kept for MIR input, no `-disable-mir-output-verify`, FailsVerification or reserved ARGUMENTS; no clang change.
- Each new test fails without its fix (items 3-5) or pins the upstream change it names (items 1, 6, 10); the curated upstream tests really exercise the hooked files; the allow-list is empty or narrow and justified per file; the manifest check cannot pass silently (shallow clone, stale entries, unmatched globs, unqualified switch cases, the base during a merge in progress); the lit verdict counts PASS only and fails on UNRESOLVED, XPASS and stale allow entries.
- The gate and CI scripts: the compile leg never deletes the hooks tree, never nests the tree's lock and never touches D:\llvm-msil\build; self-tests write nothing inside the repository; SKIP and FAIL rows are honest; CI's `-MinPass`, its gtest filter, its skipped legs and its `if:` guard are explained; lit-legs.sh's header matches its `--list`.

**Rebuild cost.** MSIL target: 15 TUs (MSILTargetMachine.cpp, MSILISelDAGToDAG.cpp and the 13 that include MSILUtilities.h, MSILArgumentMove.cpp and MSILUtilities.cpp among them), plus relinks of llc, opt, clang, MCTests and MSILTests (~10-20 min); llvm-profdata is new: llvm-profdata.cpp plus the two libraries the build lacks, LLVMDebuginfod and LLVMHTTP (6 TUs in all), and one link (est. 2-4 min, 30-60 MB on D:). The private hooks tree on C: already exists (about 460 MB; if it has to be recreated: 242 s configure plus 473 s for the ARM object, about 140 MB). The gate adds about 45-55 min to M10's ~2 h: step 13 seconds, step 14 ~2 min, steps 15-17 ~6 min, steps 18-20 under a minute, step 21 6-10 min, step 22 12-15 min, step 23 seconds, and step 24 grows by the more-levels, utc and upstream-hooks rows (~10-14 min).

### M12. Backlog fixes: whole-program aliases and weak references, empty asm with operands, inline i128 division, byval slots, Linux oracle

**Goal.** Close the backend items every Phase 2 path hits and give the gates the oracles Phase 2 needs (recon `p2/backlog.md` 2-4 and 9; brief section 2, Q33, Q34, Q36, Q38, Q39). Whole-program mode (the only mode until M19, which guards these with `isObjectMode()`, 5.8.10): an alias becomes its aliasee plus a forwarding method, an unresolved `extern_weak` symbol is null and a direct call of it traps, a `section` on a global variable is an error instead of being dropped (judge-c-fidelity J6: a `.init_array` or `.CRT$XCU` constructor silently never ran), and unreferenced `linkonce` functions are dropped before they are diagnosed (UCRT `stdio.h` at -O0). Every mode: an empty asm with operands (`black_box`) becomes a barrier that keeps its operands, i128 division and FP<->i128 conversions expand inline (Q36), aggregate `va_arg` is a diagnostic instead of a crash, byval copies share frame slots. Infrastructure (5.12.8): `-std=gnu17`, compiler-rt in the Windows oracle, the E7 Linux oracle (Q33), a private WSL .NET (Q39), lit response files, the setup-dotnet pin (Q38).

**Depends on:** M11 and the Phase 2 plan commit (plan sections 5.6 and 5.12).

**Header changes:**
- none (`MSILMachineFunctionInfo.h` is target-local: 15 MSIL TUs recompile)

**Work packages**

#### M12.a Whole-program lowerings in MSILPrepareIR and the clang asm path (implement, ~400 lines)

- Owned files: `llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILPrepareIR.cpp`, `clang/lib/CodeGen/CGStmt.cpp`
- Reads: llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/backlog.md sections 2.1, 2.3, 3.1 and 9; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/backlog-files/alias-rust/ (alias.ll, calias.c, merge.ll, lower_rust.py); llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/backlog-files/blackbox/ (bb.c, fakeuse.ll); llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/backlog-files/vaarg/vaagg.ll; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/judge-c-fidelity.md sections F4, F5 and 6.4; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/judge-c-fidelity-files/probes/p8.c; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/driver-toolchain.md section 5.4; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/p2/driver-toolchain-files/logs/hosted-probe.log; llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILUtilities.h (getPInvokeModule, isSpecialLLVMGlobal, getIRName, getILName); llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILTargetMachine.cpp (addIRPasses); llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILAsmPrinter.cpp (doInitialization, collectConstructors); llvm/lib/Target/MSIL/MSILISelLowering.cpp (VAArgUnsupported); llvm/include/llvm/IR/InlineAsm.h; llvm/docs/MSIL/recon/m11/split-files/tools/ (relink.ps1, mkrsp.py); this plan sections 2, 3 (D14, D19, D26, D36), 5.1, 5.3 (MSILUtilities.h), 5.8.10 and 5.9.6 (the trap stub msil-ld makes)
- Provides: file-static `bool lowerWholeProgramSymbols(Module &M, const TargetMachine &TM)` (aliases, `extern_weak`, sections; M19 calls it only when `!isObjectMode()`), `bool dropUnreferencedDiscardableFunctions(Module &M)`, `bool lowerEmptyInlineAsm(Function &F)`; the trap stub `@"<msil>undef_<name>"` (msil-ld's name and shape, 5.9.6); the errors `global variable @<name> in section "<section>" is not supported for MSIL yet (phase 2 CIL objects)` (pinned by M12.c's `section-errors.ll` and M12.d's `section-globals.c` until M20, which retires it: M20.a lays out named sections in whole-program output as 5.8.10 says, M20.d updates both tests, and 5.9.16's `p8-section-ctor` gives 42 on `asm` too) and, for an aggregate `va_arg`, `the va_arg instruction is not supported for MSIL yet (phase 3 variadics)`

`runOnModule`, after the target check, `resetExceptionModel` and `disableMetadataSections`, runs (1) `lowerWholeProgramSymbols`, (2) `dropUnreferencedDiscardableFunctions`, then the per-function loop, which calls (3) `lowerEmptyInlineAsm` before `diagnoseDefinition`, which gains (4); the file comment lists them. **(1a) Aliases**, backlog 2.1 steps 1-4 as amended by judge-c-fidelity F5: an alias is lowered when its aliasee object (`getAliaseeObject()`) is a defined Function, its value type a FunctionType and the offset 0, or a GlobalVariable and its value type not a FunctionType (any constant offset). Remove it from llvm.used and llvm.compiler.used, replace every use (code, initializers, llvm.global_ctors, other aliases) by `getAliasee()`, erase it. A function alias with non-local linkage first gets a forwarder with its name, function type, linkage, visibility, DLL storage class and unnamed_addr: one plain call of the aliasee object returning its result (no `musttail`, never `jmp`, which ILVerify rejects); a type mismatch is left to MSILFixFunctionBitcasts, which runs later. Any other alias (kind mismatch, offset into a function, ifunc aliasee) keeps `alias @<name> is not supported for MSIL`; ifuncs stay errors. **(1b) `extern_weak`**: a function declaration that `MSIL::getPInvokeModule(TT, MSIL::getILName(F, TM), &F)` resolves stays a P/Invoke (M15 widens that policy; this rule follows it). Otherwise its calls and invokes and the llvm.global_ctors entries naming it use the stub (internal, created once, the declaration's type, body `llvm.trap` + `unreachable`, printed `ldnull`, `throw`), every other use (compares, initializers, stored addresses, no_cfi and dso_local_equivalent wrappers) becomes `ptr null`, it leaves the used lists and stays an unused declaration. An `extern_weak` variable: every use becomes `ptr null`, then it is erased. Confirm that `MSILAsmPrinter::doInitialization` caches nothing that a function added by this pass would miss. **(1c) Sections** (F4): every GlobalVariable definition with an explicit section, except what `MSIL::isSpecialLLVMGlobal` accepts, gets the error above through `LLVMContext::emitError` (name from `getIRName`, section verbatim), in module order before any function diagnostic; the global stays ordinary data. Function sections stay ignored. **(2)** A definition with linkonce or linkonce_odr linkage that nothing uses outside its own body loses its body (`deleteBody`, comdat cleared, as a diagnosed definition does); then, repeatedly, every linkonce, linkonce_odr, internal or private definition whose last outside use was in a dropped body (driver-toolchain 5.4). Uses in initializers and the used and ctor lists count; global variables are never dropped; a local function unreferenced from the start stays (ret.ll). **(3)** Empty asm with operands: backlog 2.3's rule and lowering, precisely: a call (not invoke or callbr) of an InlineAsm whose string is empty after trimming, whose inputs are of any kind, whose outputs are indirect (`=*m`) or direct and tied to an input of the same type, any clobbers, no label; insert the D36 fence, `call void (...) @llvm.fake.use(<v>)` for each input that is not a Constant and has an integer type of at most 64 bits, a pointer, float or double type, and `call void @llvm.sideeffect()`; the result becomes the tied input (several: insertvalue from poison). Everything else keeps `inline assembly is not supported for MSIL` (add-prototypes.ll's untied `"=r,r"` included). In clang's `emitMSILAsmStmt` (`CGStmt.cpp` ~2751-2762): keep the operand-free fence; a GCCAsmStmt with a trimmed-empty string, no labels and outputs that are each read-write, tied by an input, or memory-only (TargetInfo::ConstraintInfo) goes down the native path (`AsmConstraintsInfo::EmitAsmStmt`), so its IR equals the native triple's; everything else, asm goto and Microsoft asm keep `err_msil_asm_unsupported`. **(4)** A VAArgInst of struct or array type is reported (DiagnosticInfoUnsupported, the text above, equal to `VAArgUnsupported`, which va-intrinsics.ll pins) and the body is deleted (SelectionDAGBuilder::visitVAArg crashes on it); scalar and vector `va_arg` stay with ISel. Checks: msil-syntax.ps1 on both TUs; then a private llc and clang as M11.a built them: compile the changed TUs with their compile_commands.json commands into scratch (outputs redirected), link with the line split-files/tools/mkrsp.py writes, those objects ahead of the shared build's libraries (relink.ps1), never writing D:\llvm-msil\build: backlog-files' alias.ll, calias.c, merge.ll (with `-mllvm -expand-div-rem-bits=64 -mllvm -expand-fp-convert-bits=64` for M12.b), bb.c, vaagg.ll and p8.c on both x86_64 triples at -O0/-O2, and calias.c (exit 0), bb.c (42) and merge.ll (88) run on .NET 8 through HEAD's msil-run.py (`git show HEAD:msil/utils/msil-run.py` into scratch: M12.e owns the working copy, 5.6.1 rule 7). Hand over the IL differences over msil/test/M1 and llvm/test/CodeGen/MSIL, for M12.f and the gate's fix loop (no WP of M12 waits for them).

GettingStarted.md section 7: the new legs, the private runtime and E7 on the WSL legs, host setup, `msil_native_rtlib`, response files. msil/README.md Layout: `utils/linux-oracle/`, `utils/make-linux-sysroot.py`, `utils/msil-wsl-dotnet.sh`. msil/test/README.md: `-std=gnu17`, E7 and `<stem>.linux.expected`, legs, counts. Design.md stays untouched.
